title: Social judgments of faces across world regions are predicted better by distinctiveness than masculinity
abstractText: Social judgments of faces influence important social outcomes. Although many researchers have argued that facial masculinity plays a key role in perceptions of both valenced social judgments and dominance, whether these effects are consistent among people from different world regions is highly contentious. Consequently, we investigated possible relationships between masculinity and ratings of 120 faces made by 11,484 participants from eleven world regions (Africa, Asia, Australia and New Zealand, Central America and Mexico, Eastern Europe, Middle East, Scandinavia, South America, United Kingdom, United States and Canada, Western Europe). Surprisingly, masculinity did not significantly predict either perceived valence or dominance. By contrast, facial distinctiveness (i.e., atypicality) was significantly and negatively correlated with valenced perceptions across world regions and predicted valenced perceptions better than did masculinity. Collectively, our results suggest that distinctiveness (or correlates thereof), but not masculinity, shows a consistent association with social judgments of faces across different world regions, potentially due to an “anomalous-is-bad” stereotype whereby people ascribe negative traits to individuals with atypical face shapes.

title: Color preferences in dogs: A replication study
abstractText: Free-ranging dogs ( Canis familiaris ) in India have been shown to prefer approaching yellow bowls before blue and grey ones (Roy et al. 2025. Animal Cognition , 28(1), 1–9). However, it is not clear if this preference for the color yellow is specific to free-ranging dogs in India or whether it generalizes to other dog populations. We conducted a replication of the Roy et al. study to assess whether pet dogs in the United States show similar preferences by measuring whether they approached yellow, blue, or grey bowls first. We conducted two experiments and found that pet dogs younger than seven years old first approached yellow bowls most often, replicating Roy et al.’s findings. To test if brightness rather than color accounted for this preference, we conducted a third preference experiment with light, medium, and dark grey bowls. The dogs did not prefer the light grey bowl, indicating that there was not an overall preference for brighter shades. Therefore, a preference for yellow food-related objects extends beyond free-ranging dogs to our sample of pet dogs. Understanding dog color preferences is important for guiding the design of dog products and environments but also is critical for canine behavioral scientists who must make decisions about colors for experimental stimuli.

title: VISTA Magellanic Clouds deep observations of Classical Cepheids. Precision distances and a collision-driven Small Magellanic Cloud
abstractText: The central regions of the Magellanic Clouds are crucial for understanding galaxy interactions and calibrating the cosmic distance scale, yet they remain observationally challenging due to extreme stellar crowding. We utilised deep VISTA observations (VMCDeep) to determine the highest-precision near-infrared period-luminosity (PL) and period-Wesenheit (PW) relations to date for Classical Cepheids (δ Cep class, DCEPs) in the dense central regions of the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (LMC and SMC). We analysed J and K_s time-series data covering the central 1.77 ^ deg 2 of each galaxy. Utilising approximately 40 epochs per filter and point spread function (PSF)-based photometry, we derived high-quality light curves for 573 and 2090 DCEPs in the LMC and SMC, respectively. We derived exceptionally precise PL and PW relations, exhibiting the lowest photometric dispersion published so far for the Magellanic Clouds. Fourier parameters calculated from the light curves indicate that pulsational models incorporating a mildly non-canonical mass-luminosity relation and a mixing-length parameter of α=1.7 best reproduce the observations. Age derivations confirm a bimodal star formation history in the SMC centre. Crucially, we discovered a striking line-of-sight spatial dichotomy within the young SMC DCEP population (t < 116 Myr), which is bifurcated into two distinct structures separated by ∼ 4 kpc. This provides independent stellar evidence tracing a recent direct collision with the LMC. Finally, by unifying fundamental and first-overtone pulsators, we derived a highly constrained relative distance between the Clouds. Comparing this to detached eclipsing binary distances, our data suggest a moderate metallicity correction for the Leavitt law with γ ≈ -0.2 ^ mag dex -1 .

title: Noise and quasi-periodic oscillations in black hole accretion flows
abstractText: Temporal fluctuations of the viscosity parameter at different radii in an accretion flow are known to give rise to variability in the accretion rate onto the black hole. The power spectrum of accretion-rate fluctuations is expected to exhibit a broadband power-law dependence on frequency (e.g., flicker noise). We show that viscosity fluctuations can also generate quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the power spectrum. In our model, QPOs are caused by reflection of accretion-rate fluctuations at the outer radius of the accretion flow and arise near the low-frequency break of the power spectrum, which corresponds to the inverse viscous timescale at the outer radius. These QPOs occur in geometrically thick advection-dominated accretion flows but are absent in geometrically thin cooling-dominated flows.

title: EVALUATING THE IMPACT OF DEMOGRAPHIC PROFILE ON THE USAGE OF UPI APPS IN SHIVAMOGGA DISTRICT
abstractText: In present scenario UPI payments are playing a pivotal role in digital world because of its user friendly, convenience and secure transactions. There are so many demographic and other factor influence the adoption and usage of UPI apps. This research paper focuses to evaluate the impact of Demographic profile of respondents such as qualification. Occupation and age on the usage of UPI Apps. The Primary and secondary data has been used to gather the information. The primary data are collected through structure questionnaire from 120 respondents using the Stratified Sampling technique. The study is conducted in Shivamogga District. The statistical tools such as Mediation analysis and Moderation Analysis were applied in order to find out the direct, indirect and conditional relationship among the variables. The mode of payment and frequency of usage are mediator and moderator for the study. The findings reveal that Educational Qualification and Occupation do not exert a statistically significant direct effect on UPI usage. However, both exhibit a robust indirect influence, significantly mediated by the individual’s Preferred Mode of Payment and Frequency of Usage (e.g., Bootstrap CI for Education via Mode of Pay: 0.0369 to 0.1518). Furthermore, the relationship between Age and UPI usage is found to be significantly moderated by the Preferred Mode of Payment (Interaction Term p=0.032). Specifically, the negative effect of increasing age on UPI usage diminishes as an individual’s preference for digital payment modes increases.

title: Konstruksi Peran dan Tanggung Jawab Kakak dalam Film "1 Kakak 7 Ponakan"
abstractText: Film merupakan media komunikasi massa yang dapat merepresentasikan nilai sosial dan dinamika hubungan keluarga melalui tanda-tanda audiovisual. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengidentifikasi dan mendeskripsikan makna denotasi, konotasi, dan mitos mengenai sosok kakak yang direpresentasikan melalui karakter Moko dalam film 1 Kakak 7 Ponakan. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan metode analisis semiotika Roland Barthes. Objek penelitian adalah film 1 Kakak 7 Ponakan karya Yandy Laurens, dengan tujuh adegan yang dipilih secara purposif berdasarkan keterkaitannya dengan peran dan tanggung jawab Moko terhadap keluarga. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi, dokumentasi, dan studi pustaka, kemudian dianalisis berdasarkan tiga tingkatan pemaknaan Roland Barthes. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa sosok kakak direpresentasikan melalui empat dimensi utama, yaitu sebagai pengganti orang tua dan pelindung, figur yang mengorbankan cita-cita serta menopang ekonomi keluarga, individu yang memiliki kerapuhan emosional, dan pemimpin keluarga yang mengutamakan empati. Pada tingkat mitos, film ini mengukuhkan pandangan bahwa kakak memiliki tanggung jawab melindungi dan memenuhi kebutuhan keluarga. Namun, film juga membongkar anggapan bahwa pengasuhan hanya menjadi tugas perempuan, kakak harus selalu kuat, dan kepemimpinan keluarga harus bersifat otoriter. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa makna kakak tidak hanya berkaitan dengan tuntutan pengorbanan, tetapi juga mencakup keterbatasan emosional, kepedulian, dan kebutuhan akan dukungan dalam keluarga.

title: The AI-ready teacher: Artificial intelligence literacy as a predictor of instructional innovation and teaching effectiveness among public secondary school teachers
abstractText: This study examined artificial intelligence (AI) literacy as a predictor of instructional innovation and teaching effectiveness among public secondary school teachers. Specifically, it assessed teachers’ AI literacy in terms of knowledge, skills and application, ethical and responsible use, and confidence, and determined whether AI literacy significantly predicts instructional innovation and teaching effectiveness. A quantitative predictive-correlational approach was employed, involving 101 public secondary school teachers. Data were gathered through a structured questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics and simple linear regression. The findings revealed that teachers demonstrated a high level of AI literacy, with mean scores of 4.45 in knowledge, 4.28 in skills and application, 4.42 in ethical and responsible use, and 4.26 in confidence. Regression analysis further established that AI literacy significantly and positively predicts instructional innovation (β = 0.668, p < .001), explaining 44.6% of its variance. Similarly, AI literacy significantly predicts teaching effectiveness (β = 0.304, p = .002), accounting for 9.3% of its variance. These results indicate that AI literacy has a stronger predictive association with instructional innovation than with teaching effectiveness. The findings suggest that teachers’ understanding and responsible application of AI are important considerations in promoting innovative instructional practices. However, teaching effectiveness involves broader pedagogical and professional competencies beyond technological literacy. The study highlights the need for continuous professional development, practical AI training, and institutional support to strengthen teachers’ capacity to integrate artificial intelligence responsibly and meaningfully into educational practices. It concludes that enhancing AI literacy may contribute to instructional improvement and support the development of more innovative and effective teaching practices in public secondary schools.

title: THEORETICAL INVESTIGATION OF TEMPERATURE-DEPENDENT ELECTRON TRANSFER PROCESSES AT THE D102/SNO₂ SEMICONDUCTOR INTERFACE
abstractText: This work aims to study the temperature-dependent electron transfer rate at the interface between the D102 dye and SnO₂ material within the framework of the Marcus-Gerischer model, by combining the Fermi golden rule, the Frank-Condon weighted density of states, and a connected treatment of the conduction band in SnO₂.The reorganization energy was calculated for five solvents methanol, acetonitrile, propylene carbonate, γ-butyrolactone, and dimethyl sulfoxide from their dielectric and refractive properties together with the relevant D102 and SnO₂ parameters, and ranges from 0.496 to 0.584 eV. The driving force is fixed at ∆G0 = −1.31 eV by the offset between the D102 LUMO and the SnO₂ conduction-band edge, and does not vary with solvent.With this driving force and these reorganization energies, |∆G0|/ΛADlies between 2.24 and 2.64 for every solvent studied, placing the D102/SnO₂ system in the Marcus inverted region rather than near the activationless condition. As a consequence, the rate calculation increases with reorganization energy instead of decreasing with it, so methanol gives the fastest rate and DMSO the slowest, by a factor of roughly 60 at 300 K. The rate (TDAE s−1) scales exactly with the squared electronic coupling over the eightfold range examined, and rises with temperature by a factor of 2.4 to 3.5 between 300 and 330 K mainly through the temperature dependence of the Marcus exponential term.

title: Modalities on English comprehension and retention among grade 11 HUMSS learners at Osias Educational Foundation, Inc.
abstractText: This study examined the effects of print and digital reading modalities on the English reading comprehension and retention of Grade 11 Humanities and Social Sciences (HUMSS) learners at Osias Educational Foundation, Inc. It specifically determined learners’ demographic profiles, reading preferences, and levels of comprehension and retention using the two reading modalities. The study also tested whether significant differences existed in learners’ comprehension and retention performance between print and digital reading. Findings revealed that learners generally preferred print materials, although preferences varied by sex. In terms of comprehension, learners obtained higher mean scores when reading printed texts than digital texts. Similarly, print reading yielded better retention outcomes, with 53.6% of learners obtaining an excellent rating and none classified as poor. In comparison, digital reading recorded 35.7% excellent and 7.1% poor retention ratings. Despite these differences in mean scores, statistical analysis showed no significant difference between print and digital reading modalities in terms of comprehension and retention (p greater than 0.05). Thus, the null hypotheses were accepted, indicating that both modalities can support learners’ reading development. Nevertheless, the consistent advantage of print reading highlights its potential value in promoting focused reading, comprehension, and information retention. Based on the findings, a Reading Enhancement Program was proposed, emphasizing print-based reading materials, guided annotation, story mapping, structured questioning, and reflective activities to develop higher-order thinking skills. Digital materials were likewise recommended as supplementary resources to provide learners with varied and accessible reading experiences.

title: Development of a worktext in statistics and probability 10
abstractText: This study aimed to develop and validate the Good in Numbers Worktext in Mathematics 10, focusing on the topics of Probability and Statistics for the Third Quarter of School Year 2019–2020. Specifically, it identified the challenges encountered by Grade 10 Mathematics teachers and developed an instructional material to address the identified needs. The study employed a Research and Development (R&D) design guided by the ADDIE model, consisting of Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation. Interviews were conducted with Grade 10 Mathematics teachers in the Schools Division of Candon City to identify instructional challenges, while the developed worktext was evaluated by mathematics teachers and school heads from public and private schools in Ilocos Sur using the Department of Education's Learning Resources Management and Development System (LRMDS) Evaluation Rating Sheet for Print Resources. Findings revealed four major challenges: learners, instructional materials, physical facilities, and curriculum. The developed worktext covered permutation and combination, probability of compound events, mutually and not mutually exclusive events, and probability of independent events. The validation results showed that the worktext met and exceeded the prescribed standards in terms of content, format, presentation and organization, and accuracy and up-to-datedness. The findings established that the Good in Numbers Worktext is a valid and acceptable supplementary instructional material for teaching Mathematics 10.

title: Exploring teachers perceived school attendance challenges of learners with intellectual disabilities at Adukrom Methodist Unit School in Ghana
abstractText: The purpose of the study was to explore teachers' perceived school attendance challenges of learners with intellectual disabilities at Adukrom Methodist Unit School. The study employed a qualitative research approach with a descriptive case study design. The census sampling was employed to sampled all the 6 teachers who teach learners with intellectual disabilities. The instrument used was semi structured interview guide. The study revealed that,health challenges, financial challenges on the side of parents, name-calling by peers, and long distance from home to school were how the teachers describe the challenges facing learners with intellectual disabilities and again revealed that establishing more unit schools, organizing regular PTA meetings, improved professional development for teachers and providing adequate TLRs were measures need to be put in place to address the attendance challenges of learners with intellectual disabilities. It was recommended that, various stakeholders of education of the school should effectively collaborate with each other to help address the attendance challenges of learners with intellectual disabilities.

title: Literacy level of kindergarten learners under the MATATAG curriculum: Basis for reading intervention program
abstractText: This study assessed the literacy level of kindergarten learners under the MATATAG Curriculum as a basis for developing a Reading Intervention Program. Specifically, it examined the learners’ literacy skills based on the assessments of kindergarten teachers and school administrators, the extent to which kindergarten learning objectives were achieved, and the seriousness of problems encountered in assessing learners’ literacy development. The study also evaluated the face and content validity of the research instrument. Findings revealed that the respondents were educationally qualified and experienced, with relevant professional development through their participation in trainings, seminars, and webinars related to kindergarten education. The respondents generally gave very high assessments of the learners’ literacy levels, with most indicators rated as very highly assessed and the remaining indicators rated highly assessed. Likewise, 24 of the 25 objectives of kindergarten classes were perceived to have been very highly achieved, indicating positive assessments of the implementation of the kindergarten program. However, all identified situations affecting the assessment of learners’ literacy were considered highly serious, suggesting challenges that may influence the accuracy and reliability of literacy assessment. Furthermore, the research instrument obtained very high ratings in terms of face and content validity, particularly in its appearance, language, layout, appropriateness, timeliness, functionality, acceptability, implementability, and sustainability. The findings highlight the importance of continuous literacy assessment and appropriate instructional support in kindergarten education. Based on the results, a Reading Intervention Program was proposed to strengthen foundational literacy skills and address the learning needs of kindergarten learners under the MATATAG Curriculum.

title: Analytical Hierarchical Process-based Water Quality Index Evaluation for Overall Knowledge on Spatial and Seasonal Changes of Water Quality of the Lower Stretch of River Ganga
abstractText: Water quality of a surface water body refers to the status of its water whether it can be used as potable water sources. Basic knowledge of water quality and associated methods regarding its analysis are of notable importance as ecological advantage and human wellbeing are also associated with it. But defining water quality condition of a surface water body for a single particular aspect will lead to misinterpretation of the condition status as it is open to any sort of pollution possibilities. There are many conventional techniques allied to water quality assessment for different pollution scenarios with defined water quality parameters. Despite of the availability those methods, the present study adhered to the quality index calculation with all sorts of water quality issues in an integrated way. The current study chose an important watershed to analysis water quality characteristics under the aegis of multi criteria decision making (MCDM). Locations for water sample collection along the stretch of the river were selected on the basis of population density and practices of cloth washing, bathing, utensil cleaning in the river, agricultural practices and industrial activities such as discharging effluent from industries to the adjacent portion of the river. Suitable water quality parameters were considered to define Water Quality Index (WQI). The study after all the sampling, laboratory experiments, values of different parameters and finally water quality indexing could come to a conclusion that according to the water quality scale range the river water is unsuitable for drinking without any proper treatment. Though the condition of water usually gets better in monsoon and autumn compared to winter and summer seasons but that too can?t ensure good health of the river water.

title: Urban expansion trajectories and maximum temperature dynamics across urban socio-ecological systems in the South American Tropics
abstractText: Rapid urbanization is transforming socio-ecological systems across the South American tropics, driving land-use change and altering local thermal regimes. This study analyzes the spatiotemporal dynamics of urban expansion and associated maximum temperature variations between 1985 and 2018 across 31 tropical South American cities. We examine how urban growth patterns differ according to urban hierarchy (global, sub-global, regional-subglobal transition, and regional cities) and how these dynamics interact with climatic, topographic, ecological, demographic, and economic factors. A geospatial database integrating remote sensing, climatic, topographic, ecological, demographic, and economic datasets was developed to assess urban expansion trajectories and temperature dynamics. Urban growth and its drivers were analyzed using two-way ANOVA, k-means clustering, correlation analysis, multinomial logit models, and Random Forest classification. Urban expansion differed significantly among city categories. Global cities exhibited episodic phases of accelerated growth, whereas sub-global and regional cities followed more continuous expansion trajectories, with a generalized intensification during 2014–2018. Maximum temperature increased across all altitudinal ranges, although warming was not uniform across the landscape. The greatest thermal changes were concentrated in low- and intermediate-altitude urban environments, suggesting that the thermal effects of urban expansion are strongly conditioned by topographic context. Recently urbanized areas also exhibited distinct thermal conditions from long-established urban cores, consistent with spatially differentiated urban heat island processes. The explanatory models indicate that urban expansion is shaped by interacting environmental and socioeconomic factors. Early urban growth was more strongly associated with lower elevations, whereas recent expansion increasingly occurred on steeper and more rugged terrain. Urban growth was also associated with areas characterized by high forest cover and active deforestation, suggesting an expanding urban frontier within ecologically transformed landscapes. Population density and population growth were positively associated with urban expansion, while GDP exhibited a negative relationship. Random Forest results identified precipitation, GDP, altitude, and maximum temperature as the most influential predictors of urban growth. These findings demonstrate that urban expansion patterns are closely linked to thermal change across tropical South America and that warming is conditioned by topographic context rather than occurring uniformly across the landscape. Incorporating topographic, ecological, and thermal gradients into urban planning could help mitigate climate related risks and support more sustainable urban development trajectories.

Integrated optimization of the inventory routing problem under logistics collaboration and heterogeneous customer segments
abstractText: Collaborative supply chain management is essential for businesses seeking to stay competitive and enhance operational effectiveness. Customer segmentation also stands out as an essential strategy in supply chain management, providing substantial advantages. Companies can improve customer satisfaction and loyalty by providing customized services that meet the unique preferences and needs of different groups of customers. This study introduces a mathematical model for the inventory routing problem, considering demand uncertainty, heterogeneous customer segments, and their collaborative efforts. The main decisions are centered on optimizing channel selection, distribution planning, and inventory replenishment strategies of customers classified into different segments. To efficiently solve large‐scale instances of the proposed problem, two complementary heuristic solution approaches are developed: a matheuristic with local branching and a mixed‐integer programming–based heuristic that serves as a benchmark for comparison. These approaches are designed to balance solution quality and computational efficiency while capturing the complex interactions between routing, inventory, and collaboration decisions. The results of the study highlight the strategic importance of heterogeneous customer segments and collaboration in inventory routing problems. The study provides a detailed account of the benefits of establishing mutually beneficial collaborations, especially for companies with complex distribution networks serving different customer segments.

title: K-CIRCT: A Layered, Composable, and Executable Formal Semantics for CIRCT Dialects
abstractText: CIRCT (Circuit Intermediate Representations Compilers and Tools) is an open-source compiler infrastructure that provides a unified toolchain and reusable intermediate representations for multiple hardware description languages (HDLs) across the phases of hardware design. Despite its growing adoption, CIRCT lacks formal semantics. We present K-CIRCT, the first formal semantic framework for CIRCT that enables RISC-V processor design formalization. To match CIRCT’s extensible architecture, we introduce a layered semantic framework: (1) the MLIR infrastructure layer, extensible for different MLIR-based domain compilers; (2) the CIRCT hardware layer for hardware-specific semantics, and (3) dialect-specific layers for individual CIRCT dialects. Using this framework, we formalized the semantics of the hw , comb , seq , and sv dialects with concise definitions. The framework ensures dialect composability through effectful functions, crucial for practical multi-dialect designs. K-CIRCT enables the generation of interpreters and formal verifiers for CIRCT. Based on the interpreter, we developed a simulator and validated K-CIRCT by simulating the well-known Rocket Chip RISC-V design. Our validation confirms the correctness and adequacy of our semantics for real-world hardware designs.

title: Text-Free Multi-domain Graph Pre-training: Toward Graph Foundation Models
abstractText: Graphs arise across a wide spectrum of real-world applications, spanning biology, e-commerce, social networks, and more. This ubiquity naturally raises a fundamental question: Can we build a graph foundation model that leverages knowledge from multiple domains and generalizes effectively to entirely new ones? Achieving this goal, however, is challenging due to the substantial variation in graph characteristics across domains. While early efforts have explored cross-domain graph pre-training, many rely on auxiliary textual data to bridge semantic gaps between graphs, limiting their applicability to text-attributed graphs. In addition, integrating multiple source domains can introduce domain conflicts and uneven relevance to the target task, ultimately hindering robust generalization. To overcome these challenges, we propose MDGPT , a text-free graph learning framework that unifies and transfers knowledge across different graph domains. We begin by introducing a set of domain tokens that align diverse features from various domains, enabling coherent representation learning during pre-training. Then, we develop a two-stage prompting mechanism: the unifying prompt encodes domain-invariant semantics shared across multiple sources, while the mixing prompt selectively composes domain-specific signals to adapt the model to the target domain. We evaluate our approach on six benchmark datasets, where MDGPT achieves up to a 10.2% improvement over state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating its effectiveness in cross-domain generalization. (Codes are available at https://github.com/Nashchou/MDGPT .)

title: What is the Role of Small Models in the LLM Era: A Survey
abstractText: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in various reasoning tasks, which leads to the development of increasingly large models. However, scaling up model sizes results in significantly higher computational costs and energy consumption, which makes these models impractical for academic researchers and businesses with limited resources. At the same time, Small Models (SMs) are frequently used in practical settings, although their significance is currently underestimated. This raises important questions about the role of SMs in the era of LLMs, a topic that has received limited attention in prior surveys. In this work, we systematically examine the relationship between LLMs and SMs from two key perspectives: Collaboration and Competition ( or Complementarity ). We hope this survey provides valuable insights for practitioners, fostering a deeper understanding of the contribution of small models and promoting more efficient use of computational resources. Code and additional resources for this survey are available at: https://github.com/tigerchen52/awesome_role_of_small_models.

Maximal number of mixed Nash equilibria in generic games where each player has two pure strategies
abstractText: The number of Nash equilibria of the mixed extension of a generic finite game in normal form is finite and odd. This raises the question how large the number can be, depending on the number of players and the numbers of their pure strategies. Here we present a lower bound for the maximal possible number in the case of n -player games where each player has two pure strategies. It is surprisingly close to a known upper bound.

title: A differences-in-differences study of staff experience in the English NHS after investment in digital technologies
abstractText: Background: England’s National Health Service invests in digital technologies to improve productivity, but their effects on staff experience are uncertain. We assess whether funding through the 2021–22 Digital Productivity Programme is associated with changes in staff morale and engagement. Methods: We combine programme funding records with organisation-level National Health Service Staff Survey data for 103 Acute and Acute and Community Trusts from 2018 to 2023. A two-way fixed-effects difference-in-differences design compares 26 funded and 77 unfunded trusts before funding (2018–2021) and after funding (2022–2023). Event-study models assess pre-treatment trends, and entropy balancing addresses measured baseline differences. Results: Here we show that overall programme funding has no association with most outcomes and is marginally associated with a less favourable thinking-about-leaving score ( − 0.06, 95% confidence interval −0.14 to 0.01; p = 0.09). Automation and artificial intelligence funding shows no detectable associations. Real-time location system funding is associated with less favourable stressors, engagement, motivation and involvement scores. Virtual reality results are not reported because pre-treatment trends are inconsistent. Conclusions: The associations between digital investment and staff experience differ by technology type. These findings support technology-specific evaluation and staff-focused implementation, while residual unobserved selection and the short follow-up period limit causal interpretation.

title: Foster Care or In‐Home Support: Differences in Mental Health Treatment, Education and Crime
abstractText: This study traces the trajectories of children before and after their first involvement with Child Welfare Services (CWS), comparing outcomes for those placed in foster care with those who received home‐based services. Leveraging administrative data covering more than 2 decades, we follow these children from infancy through childhood and into adulthood, tracking outcomes in health, education, crime, welfare dependence, and labor market participation. We follow children around the time of their initial CWS contact. We show that children placed in foster care are substantially more likely to receive mental health treatment in the years following the first intervention, with the increase substantially larger for girls than for boys. In contrast, we observe only modest later differences between the two groups across other outcomes. Using geographical variation in the likelihood of being assigned to foster care, we corroborate the finding that foster care placement increases mental healthcare use. One interpretation of this pattern is that foster care placement compensates for childhood adversity by improving access to mental health care services.

title: What Kind of Suffering Does Meditation Reduce?
abstractText: Meditation has been shown to reduce various forms of suffering and increase well-being. However, its broad effectiveness raises the question: In what way does meditation reduce suffering? We explore this question systematically, proposing that meditation’s effectiveness stems not from addressing specific types of suffering but from dismantling underlying mechanisms that create the conditions for suffering. First, we examine suffering from three frameworks: well-being (hedonia/eudaimonia), contemporary mindfulness (non-reactivity), and traditional Buddhist practice (ignorance). While these approaches may correspond to phenomenologically similar states with less suffering, they reinforce different underlying habits, thereby affecting the likelihood of future suffering. Second, we clarify this distinction by drawing on the action–perception cycle from a computational phenomenology perspective. Particularly, we cast suffering as self-reinforcing action–perception cycles, and unreliable/reliable reduction of suffering as unstable/stable equilibrium in action–perception cycles. Third, we propose four stages through which meditation facilitates a reliable reduction by progressively revealing that suffering, typically perceived as a passive experience, is in fact a specific pattern of action we are engaged in (i.e. meditation provides a reliable way to reduce enacted suffering). Our framework provides a conceptual foundation for mathematically formalizing and computationally modelling non-reactivity, ignorance (in the Buddhist sense), and suffering, and has implications for the larger goal of understanding perception, action, and conscious experience.

title: Temperature and time dependence of cellulose solution stability in combined aqueous hydroxide bases
abstractText: Cellulose solutions in aqueous hydroxide bases often display an intriguing and limited stability over time and within a limited temperature range. Our previous studies pointed out a synergistic effect of combining two hydroxide bases, NaOH and tetramethylammonium hydroxide (TMAH) on stability over time at a molar ratio of 50/50. Here, we hypothesise that the delayed gelation of cellulose in this system is related to the ability of the base combination to disturb the formation of a stable monobase-cellulose salt during aggregation. We combine studies addressing time and temperature dependency of the solution stability with X-ray diffraction and solid-state NMR studies of swollen cellulose to address the hypothesis. The results showed that the dissolution window at low temperatures turned out to be similar for the individual and combined bases. However, increased stability over time was observed in the 50/50 NaOH/TMAH(aq) compared to the individual base solutions, and could be related to different crystal structures observed in swollen model samples.

title: Sustained delivery of mGnRHa and domperidone using two distinct PLGA microsphere formulations enhances spermiation in goldfish (Carassius auratus)
abstractText: Artificial reproduction in fish species with strong dopaminergic inhibition typically relies on acute hormone injections, while controlled-release strategies remain underutilized. This study aimed to develop, for the first time, separately encapsulated microspheres of mGnRHa and domperidone using a PLGA polymer matrix for spermiation induction in male goldfish ( Carassius auratus ), serving as a dopaminergic species model. Microspheres were synthesized via single and double emulsion techniques. The entrapment efficiencies of mGnRHa and DOM microspheres were 94.48% and 98.21%, respectively. Forty adult males were randomly divided into four groups: negative control (empty microspheres), positive control (acute injection of 5 µg/kg b.w. mGnRHa + 2.5 mg/kg b.w. DOM), M10 and M20; microspheres containing 10 µg/kg b.w. mGnRHa + 5 mg/kg b.w. DOM, and 20 µg/kg b.w. + 10 mg/kg b.w. DOM, respectively. Spermatogenic parameters were evaluated at 24, 72 h, and 10 days post-injection. Sustained-release treatments (M10 and M20) significantly enhanced sperm volume, spermatocrit, density, motility, and viability compared to control groups ( P < 0.05). Improvements were most pronounced in M20, particularly at 10 days. These results demonstrate that PLGA-based microspheres containing mGnRHa and DOM, when encapsulated separately, are a promising alternative to conventional hormone therapies, offering enhanced and prolonged spermiation in species with dopaminergic inhibition.

HER2 and YAP co-expression amplifies an autocrine growth-factor program that confers growth-factor independence in HER2-positive breast cancer
abstractText: HER2-targeted therapies have improved outcomes in HER2-positive breast cancer, yet ~ 20% of tumours recur within five years and the mechanisms underlying the aggressive, treatment-resistant subset are incompletely defined. The Hippo-pathway effector YAP is implicated in this subset; here we explored the mechanistic role of YAP in HER2-driven aggressive oncogenic features using cell lines as a model system. We examined YAP expression by immunohistochemistry in 76 HER2-positive primary breast tumours with clinical follow-up. To dissect mechanism, we generated MCF10A mammary epithelial cell lines stably overexpressing HER2 and/or YAP and shYAP lines in both the parental and the HER2 background, and characterised proliferation, migration and signalling in complete and in growth-factor-reduced media. Whole-transcriptome RNA-sequencing was performed across all eight engineered lines. Combination treatments with verteporfin, dasatinib, trastuzumab and lapatinib were tested in SKBR3 and ZR-75-1 cells; YAP-target growth-factor transcripts were measured by RT-qPCR. In the patient cohort, high YAP expression showed numerical trends toward aggressive features (residual disease after NACT, recurrence, shorter disease-free survival), though none reached statistical significance in this underpowered cohort. In MCF10A, HER2 + YAP co-expression produced a significant but modest cooperative effect on proliferation and migration under standard growth conditions. Under growth-factor-reduced conditions, the cooperation became markedly synergistic, consistent with acquisition of autocrine self-sufficiency. YAP knockdown in the HER2 background reversed the proliferation and migration phenotypes and sensitised cells to trastuzumab. RNA-sequencing identified 238 genes synergistically up-regulated by HER2 + YAP and reversed by YAP knockdown, heavily enriched for autocrine growth factors (AREG, IL6, FSTL1, CCN1, CCN2/CTGF), chemokines and extracellular matrix components. In SKBR3 and ZR-75-1 cells, combined verteporfin + trastuzumab produced greater growth inhibition than either agent alone with concomitant down-regulation of the same autocrine growth factors. We describe a co-regulated YAP–HER2 transcriptional output that amplifies an autocrine growth-factor loop, as a candidate mechanism for the aggressive subset of HER2-positive disease with high YAP expression. These data provide preclinical rationale for combined YAP and HER2 inhibition; they do not establish a validated co-targetable vulnerability. Validation in HER2-amplified and trastuzumab-resistant models, in vivo, and ultimately in patients stratified by YAP expression is required.

title: Large smooth twins from short lattice vectors
abstractText: Finding the largest pair of consecutive B -smooth integers for a fixed B , also called a B -smooth twin, is computationally challenging. It has only been provably done for $$B \le 100$$ B ≤ 100 and heuristically for $$100 < B \le 113$$ 100 < B ≤ 113 . We improve this by detailing a new algorithm to find such smooth twins based on solving the shortest vector problem (SVP) in a well-constructed lattice. Using an estimate of the largest B -smooth twin that we develop in this work, we are able to significantly increase B and notably report the heuristically largest twin with $$B = 751$$ B = 751 , which has 196 bits. By slightly modifying the lattice, we are able to find even larger twins, but the resulting smoothness bound will not always be optimal. This notably includes a 213-bit twin with $$B = 997$$ B = 997 , which is the largest twin found in this work.

title: Diet composition, staple-food dependence and structural patterns of dietary diversity: a global analysis using FAOSTAT food balance sheet data
abstractText: Dietary diversity is a key indicator of nutritional adequacy and a crucial component of sustainable food systems. Nonetheless, the roles of plant- and animal-derived foods in shaping dietary diversity outcomes at national and global levels are still not fully understood. Using the FAOSTAT dataset and the Simpson diversity index, this study examines the association between plant-derived food-energy share and national dietary diversity. We use 2015–2017 FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheet (FBS) data covering 182 countries. Country-level dietary diversity was calculated using the Simpson index, and its association with the plant-derived share of food energy was assessed using Pearson’s correlation coefficient. Plant-derived food-energy share was significantly negatively associated with Simpson diversity ( r = − 0.485, p < 0.01). Several countries in sub-Saharan Africa combined a high plant-derived energy share of 90% with Simpson scores of 0.90. Nevertheless, their national food-energy supplies were often concentrated in a small number of leading foods, with the five largest contributors accounting for 65–75% of available energy. By contrast, European and North American nations achieved similarly high Simpson scores of 0.90–0.95 through a less concentrated distribution of energy across cereals, animal-derived foods, oils, sweeteners and other food groups. These contrasting patterns reveal a structural dietary diversity paradox in which similar numerical scores represent conceptually different situations. We describe a high score that coexists with marked staple-food concentration as absolute diversity , whereas qualitative diversity denotes a high numerical score accompanied by broader and more balanced food-group composition. The findings demonstrate that diet diversity should be interpreted alongside staple concentration and food-group composition. This approach could consequently support more cautious nutrition-security monitoring and more context-sensitive policies relating to Sustainable Development Goal 2.

title: Conservation implications for endangered Euhadra murayamai, restricted to a large-scale limestone cliff: insights from genome-wide SNPs and morphological analyses
abstractText: Rapid biodiversity loss necessitates accurate taxonomic classification and the definition of conservation units for effective management. Here, we investigated the genetic and morphological distinctiveness of the endangered land snail Euhadra murayamai, endemic to Mt. Myojo, Japan, and its relationship with the closely related species E. quaesita. Genome-wide SNPs from double digest restriction site-associated DNA sequencing (ddRAD-seq) and detailed morphological measurements were obtained. Our analyses revealed clear genetic differentiation between E. murayamai and E. quaesita, challenging previous inferences based solely on mitochondrial markers. Moreover, we detected significant genetic differentiation within E. murayamai populations across low and middle elevations, as evidenced by distinct clustering in fastStructure, a phylogenetic network and principal component analysis, as well as a high FST value. Morphological results aligned with these findings, showing significant differences in shell width and morphology between elevational populations. Approximate Bayesian computation analysis supported a scenario without gene flow after divergence and estimated interspecific divergence at approximately 85,000 generations ago and intraspecific divergence at approximately 35,000 generations ago. These results indicate that limited dispersal and elevational isolation have promoted local adaptation, underscoring the necessity for elevation-specific conservation units. Furthermore, the urgency of incorporating comprehensive genetic and morphological data into conservation planning is emphasised, thereby providing crucial insights for resolving taxonomic uncertainties and guiding effective strategies. Overall, we underscore the importance of integrating high-resolution genetic markers with morphological data to inform conservation strategies for species with restricted distributions and complex evolutionary histories.

Structural basis for constitutive activation of oncogenic gp130 mutants found in human inflammatory hepatocellular adenomas
abstractText: Inflammatory hepatocellular adenomas (IHCAs) are benign liver tumors primarily driven by somatic mutations in the gp130 receptor, resulting in its constitutive activation. To uncover the structural mechanisms underlying this activation, we employ cryo-electron microscopy and mutagenesis to study five representative IHCAs-associated gp130 mutants and two engineered mutants with ligand-independent activity. Most mutants form “X”-shaped dimers through a 3D domain-swapping mechanism, characterized by large separations between juxtamembrane domains and reliant on D1 domain-mediated “tip-to-tip” interactions for dimer clustering and activation. A rare mutant displays a distinct “Y”-shaped dimer conformation, with closely aligned juxtamembrane domains enabling direct activation independent of dimer clustering. These findings highlight the diversity of gp130 mutant activation mechanisms and provide a foundation for developing therapeutic strategies targeting aberrant gp130 signaling in IHCAs.

title: In vivo models for rustrela virus (RusV) infection in potential reservoir and spill-over hosts
abstractText: Rustrela virus (RusV; species Rubivirus strelense) is a recently discovered relative of the human rubella virus (Rubivirus rubellae) and causes fatal non-suppurative meningoencephalomyelitis in a broad range of domestic, wild and zoo mammals, in Europe and the USA, including ‘staggering disease’ in domestic cats. Based on its reportedly broad host range, a zoonotic potential of RusV cannot be excluded. Apparently healthy yellow-necked field mice (Apodemus flavicollis) and wood mice (Apodemus sylvaticus) were identified as potential reservoir hosts.In this study, we experimentally inoculated wood mice and Lewis rats with brain homogenates of RusV-infected animals. Intracranial as well as combined intranasal/peroral inoculation resulted in apparently persistent RusV infection in both rodent species, while combined intramuscular/subcutaneous injection failed to establish a detectable infection. Viral RNA loads were highest in the central nervous system, but viral RNA was prominently found also in mucosal organs of wood mice. Viral RNA was frequently detected in oral swabs from infected wood mice, but only sparsely from rats. Neither wood mice nor rats presented neurological signs during twelve weeks after inoculation. However, RusV-infected rats showed significantly reduced body weight. A lymphohistiocytic meningoencephalomyelitis was observed in infected rats, whereas infected wood mice infrequently developed minimal lesions in the brain.Our study provides the first infection model for RusV and indicates that natural infection may occur via mucosal routes. Shedding of viral RNA suggests wood mice to serve as natural reservoir hosts. In rats, we could reproduce a lymphohistiocytic meningoencephalomyelitis, as described for diseased cats and other tentative non-reservoir hosts.

title: Deciphering the role of brainstem vestibular‐related inhibitory networks in shaping postural reflexes in the Xenopus tadpole
abstractText: Brainstem vestibulospinal (VS) nuclei generate excitatory commands in response to multi‐modality sensory inputs, to activate specific spinal networks and generate adapted postural reflexes. Comparably organized in all species, bilaterally‐distributed excitatory VS nuclei with both ipsi‐ and contralateral projections alone fail to explain the mostly unilateral reflex responses typically observed. Consequently, we investigated the role of central vestibular inhibitory circuits in the functional organization of vestibular‐driven postural reflexes. Then, using a larval Xenopus brainstem/spinal cord in vitro preparation, we show that the spinal responses evoked by galvanic vestibular stimulation are shaped by both commissural and local inhibitory brainstem networks. We further show that a complex interaction between GABAergic and glycinergic inhibitory networks regulate VS neuron excitability and, consequently, the expression of the spinal response. Our data reveal that, although excitatory VS neurons execute the neural score, inhibitory neurons in the central vestibular system co‐ordinate and modulate the overall performance. image Key points Excitatory vestibulospinal (VS) pathways alone fail to explain reflex postural adjustments. VS neurons receive massive GABA and glycine inputs, both from local and commissural vestibular‐related brainstem neurons. Perturbing either inhibitory influence specifically modulates vestibular‐evoked spinal reflexes, and commissural integrity is mandatory for proper VS‐evoked reflex expression. Both local and commissural neurons regulate VS excitability via complex inhibitory interactions. Our study demonstrates the critical role of brainstem vestibular‐related inhibitory circuits in shaping spinal postural responses.

Toggling Stiffness via Multistability
abstractText: Mechanical metamaterials enable unconventional and programmable mechanical responses through structural design rather than material composition. In this work, we introduce a multistable mechanical metamaterial that exhibits a toggleable stiffness effect in which the effective shear stiffness switches discretely between stable mechanical configurations. Mechanical analysis of surrogate beam models of the unit cell reveals that this behavior originates from the rotation transmitted by the support beams to the curved beam, governing the balance between bending and axial deformation. Consequently, the shear stiffness ratio between the two states of the unit cell can be tuned by varying the slenderness of the support beams or by incorporating localized hinges that modulate rotational transfer. Experiments and 3D FEM simulations on 3D‐printed mechanical metamaterials confirm consistent stiffness toggling across geometrical variations investigated here. Finally, we demonstrate a monolithic soft clutch that leverages this effect to achieve programmable, stepwise stiffness modulation. This work identifies and characterizes a mechanism for toggleable stiffness modulation exploring multistable metamaterials, with potential applications in soft robotics and adaptive structures.

title: CrSe2 and CrTe2 Monolayers as Efficient Nanosensors for Air Pollutants
abstractText: Nanosensors are critical in environmental monitoring, industrial safety, and public health by detecting specific hazardous gases such as CO, NO, SO2, and CH4 at trace levels. This study uses density functional theory (DFT) calculations to examine the gas-sensing capabilities of chromium diselenide (CrSe2) and chromium ditelluride (CrTe2) monolayers through their structural and electronic responses to gas adsorption. Adsorption energy (Eads) analysis shows that Te vacancy-induced CrTe2 (VTe-CrTe2) exhibits the strongest binding with energies of −1.52, −1.79, and −1.61 eV for CO, NO, and SO2, respectively. Similarly, pristine CrSe2 exhibits moderate Eads values of −1.13, −1.17, −0.90, and −1.12 eV for CO, NO, SO2, and CH4, respectively; while room-temperature recovery remains prolonged for CO, NO, and CH4(τ ∼ 106–107s), practical sensor reversibility is readily achievable under mild thermal activation (up to 400 K). This study also investigates how substitutional doping of Ge, Sb, and Sn influences the sensing mechanism of CrSe2 and CrTe2 monolayers. Density of states (DOS) analysis highlights notable electronic changes around the Fermi level, especially in VTe-CrTe2 and Sb/Sn-doped CrTe2, confirming their enhanced sensing abilities. Charge density difference analysis shows significant charge redistribution, with CrTe2 experiencing stronger charge transfer effects than CrSe2. Variations in electrostatic potential and work function further demonstrate the higher sensitivity of CrTe2, particularly in its defective and doped forms, confirming its status as a superior material for gas-sensing applications.

title: A free energy principle account of musical valence, arousal, and emotionality
abstractText: Musical emotions appear to be evoked through predictions about upcoming sounds. Some studies have proposed that based on the free energy (FE) principle, which posits that the human perceives so as to minimize FE, (variational) FE dynamics are related to emotion elicitation under predictive processing. The present study investigated whether musical emotions are elicited by the realization of an expected reduction in FE through a subsequent smaller prediction error that occurs during perceptual inferences while listening to music. In a four-chord progression, the degree of expected FE reduction (larger/smaller) and subsequent prediction error size (larger/smaller) were manipulated at the third and fourth positions, respectively. In an online experiment, 200 participants rated their valence, arousal, and emotionality (a state of being emotionally engaged) upon hearing the third and fourth chords. Afterward, they clicked on a body-map region corresponding to the bodily location where they experienced a physical sensation when listening to the chord. When a larger FE reduction was expected, a subsequent chord with a smaller prediction error elicited stronger pleasure, arousal, and head sensation than a chord with a larger prediction error, which reflects the realized larger FE reduction. These findings suggest that an FE reduction may underlie emotion elicitation while listening to music.

Behavioural Lapses and Microbial Pollution Compromise the Public Health Outcomes of Safe Sanitation in Sustainable Cities
abstractText: The persistence of diarrheal diseases in urban areas, even those with ostensibly safe water and sanitation systems, indicates significant underlying microbial and infrastructural vulnerabilities that pose challenges to sustainable urban development. Kavaratti Island in India serves as a pertinent example: despite achieving universal access to desalinated water and sanitation facilities, the island reports between 250 and 500 cases of acute diarrheal disease annually. This study employs a combination of household surveys and environmental monitoring to investigate the behavioural determinants of exposure and microbial contamination across various water sources, including groundwater, ponds, and adjacent coastal waters. The findings reveal that only a quarter of households depend solely on desalinated water, while the majority continue to utilize untreated groundwater, thereby reflecting a limited understanding of the associated microbial risks. Quantitative real-time PCR analysis indicates widespread fecal contamination, with concentrations of Escherichia coli surpassing 1,000 gene copies per milliliter in all surveyed ponds and in most groundwater sources during the dry season. Furthermore, Vibrio cholerae was detected in 85% of pond samples and in 20% of groundwater samples during the rainy season. Notably, more than half of the E. coli isolates, along with all Vibrio isolates, displayed resistance to ampicillin, which is a commonly prescribed antibiotic in the region. These results illustrate that infrastructure alone is insufficient to guarantee microbial safety in vulnerable coastal urban settings. The high incidence of diarrheal disease, combined with microbial pollution and antibiotic resistance, highlights the urgent need for integrated surveillance systems, enhanced public awareness, and participatory water management strategies. Community-based initiatives, such as citizen science programs and water clinics, have the potential to strengthen public health resilience in these contexts.

title: Trends in Student Perceptions of School Connectedness from 2001 to 2024: Context Before and Immediately After the Implementation of the Whole School Approach to Emotional and Mental Wellbeing in Wales
abstractText: School connectedness is an important protective factor for young people’s mental health, however, there is an absence of analyses exploring how it has changed over time in primary and secondary schools. This is considered here in the context of the introduction of the Welsh Government Framework for Embedding a Whole School Approach to Emotional and Mental Wellbeing. Time trends analysis of six measures of school connectedness was undertaken using data from ​large, nationally representative primary school (2019–2024; n = 26,675 students) and secondary school (2001–2023; n = 503,059 students) surveys in Wales. Multilevel models were used to explore the impact of time and demographic variables (gender, age, family affluence) on each outcome (staff-student relationships, student relationships, student involvement in decision-making, liking school, school belonging and having an adult to confide in at school). The analysis found significant evidence of declines in school connectedness over time in primary and secondary schools. Girls tended to have significantly better outcomes than boys in primary school, but significantly worse in secondary and this latter effect was widening over time. Family affluence effects were more pronounced in secondary schools than primary schools, and suggested having higher family affluence was typically associated with more positive perceptions of school. School connectedness tended to decline with increasing student age. There was no evidence of improvements post-introduction of the Whole School Approach. This study offers an important, novel perspective on how school connectedness has declined over time in primary and secondary schools in Wales. It provides an important context to the introduction of statutory guidance requiring schools to introduce a whole school approach to emotional and mental wellbeing in 2021.

title: Distinct Treg-Mediated Cardiac Remodeling in HFpEF Mice Treated With Neonatal Mesenchymal Stem Cells and Their Secretome
abstractText: Background Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains a major therapeutic challenge due to its complex pathophysiology and pronounced heterogeneity. Regenerative approaches using neonatal mesenchymal stromal cells (nMSCs) and their secretome (SEC) have shown promise in other heart failure contexts. Objectives However, the effect of these therapies in HFpEF, and the underlying molecular mechanisms and causal pathways remain poorly understood. Methods HFpEF was established in two distinct murine models, followed by treatment with either nMSCs or SEC. Functional and histological endpoints were assessed. We developed a novel machine learning framework, VIPcell, which integrates data augmentation, Partial Least Squares (PLS) regression, and causal structure inference to identify genes causally linked to cardiac function using single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) data. VIPcell was applied to heart tissues from treated HFpEF animals to uncover key regulators of cardiac remodeling. Results Both nMSC and SEC therapies significantly improved diastolic function in two independent rodent HFpEF models. These improvements were associated with reduced inflammation, attenuated myocardial fibrosis, and improved exercise capacity. Intercellular communication analysis revealed widespread, system-level signaling in nMSC-treated hearts, compared to more localized endothelial–cardiomyocyte crosstalk in SEC-treated hearts. Causal inference via VIPcell suggested overlapping upstream regulators in both treatment groups, particularly genes involved in regulatory T cell (T reg ) biology and immunomodulatory signaling pathways, including FOXO signaling, NLRP3 inflammasome inhibition, and Tie2 activation. In vivo validation confirmed selective expansion of T regs following nMSC and SEC therapy. In vitro, nMSCs induced significantly greater T reg expansion compared to multiple adult stem cell types. Critically, chemical depletion of T regs abrogated the therapeutic effects of both treatments, establishing T regs as central mediators of diastolic function recovery in the HFpEF preclinical model. Conclusions nMSC and SEC therapies improve diastolic function in HFpEF through distinct remodeling mechanisms converging on T reg -mediated immune modulation. VIPcell supported identification of causal regulators, highlighting T reg -related signaling as a key driver of myocardial recovery in HFpEF. These findings offer mechanistic insight into cellular therapies for HFpEF and support the development of targeted, T reg -focused interventions.

title: Lessons from the world’s largest hepatitis C elimination program: impact on primary liver cancer burden in Egypt: a global burden of disease analysis with 2050 projections
abstractText: Introduction Primary liver cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with Egypt representing a uniquely high-burden setting due to historically widespread hepatitis C virus infection. This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate long-term trends in the burden of Primary liver cancer in Egypt from 1990 to 2023, with particular emphasize on the impact of the national HCV elimination campaign, and project future trends through 2050. Methods Data were obtained from the Global Burden of Disease 2023 database. Age-standardized incidence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), together with prevalence rates, for Primary liver cancer were analyzed by sex and underlying etiology. Future projections to 2050 were generated using the GBD forecasting framework. Results Between 1990 and 2023, age-standardized incidence, mortality, and DALY rates for PLC in Egypt declined overall, with the steepest reductions observed between 2014 and 2019, coinciding with nationwide HCV eradication efforts. However, a rebound in incidence and mortality was observed after 2019. HCV remained the leading cause of Primary liver cancer mortality throughout the study period, although its contribution declined substantially. Notably, nonalcoholic steatohepatitis surpassed hepatitis B as the second leading cause of Primary liver cancer mortality by 2009. Projections suggest that comprehensive control of viral and metabolic risk factors could reduce Primary liver cancer mortality by nearly half by 2050. Conclusion Egypt’s HCV elimination campaign substantially reduced the burden of Primary liver cancer; however, long-term surveillance and integrated, multi-etiologic prevention strategies are essential to achieve durable reductions in Primary liver cancer burden.

title: KD4MT: A Survey of Knowledge Distillation for Machine Translation
abstractText: Knowledge Distillation (KD) as a research area has gained a considerable traction in recent years as a compression tool to address challenges related to ever-larger models in NLP. Remarkably, Machine Translation (MT) offers a much more nuanced take on this narrative: in MT, KD also functions as a general-purpose knowledge transfer mechanism that shapes supervision and translation quality as well as efficiency. This survey synthesizes KD for MT (KD4MT) across 105 papers. We begin by introducing both MT and KD for non-experts, followed by an overview of the standard KD approaches relevant to MT applications. Subsequently, we categorize advances in the KD4MT literature based on (i) their methodological contributions and (ii) their practical applications. Our qualitative and quantitative analyses identify common trends in the field and highlight key research gaps as well as the absence of unified evaluation practice for KD methods in MT. We further provide practical guidelines for selecting a KD method in concrete settings and highlight potential risks associated with the application of KD to MT such as increased hallucination and bias amplification. Finally, we discuss the role of LLMs in re-shaping the KD4MT field. To support further research, we complement our survey with a publicly available database summarizing the main characteristics of the surveyed KD methods and a glossary of key terms.

title: Waste or tool? Combined use-wear analysis of Mesolithic knapped stone and shell tools in Asturias (northern Iberia)
abstractText: Technology is a fundamental social and cultural actor in the relationship between humans and non-human environments. In coastal environments, anthropologists and archaeologists have long debated the role of technological adaptations in the exploitation of marine and littoral resources. Although functionalist and evolutionary models are now largely abandoned, our knowledge of the specific technological choices made by coastal hunter-gatherer groups along the Atlantic European Holocene seaboard remains limited. Dated between 10700 and 6700 cal BP, the Asturian Mesolithic technological system has traditionally been characterized by the predominance of pebble tools and the scarcity of retouched knapped implements. However, unretouched knapped blanks and shells are seldom considered part of the so-called “Asturian toolkit.” In this paper, we address the function of Asturian knapped and shell tools as complementary components of a broader technological system. Use-wear analyses were conducted on lithic and shell assemblages from El Mazo and El Toral III (Asturias, northern Spain). The results demonstrate that unretouched lithics and shells were not merely production debris but were frequently employed as tools. Moreover, the study reveals a functional complementarity between the two raw materials. Certain activities were consistently associated with specific materials and distinct working kinematics. Shell tools appear to have been primarily used for scraping plant fibres, whereas knapped tools were preferentially employed in working bone and mineral matter, and, to a lesser extent, in processing soft animal tissues. These results open new avenues for discussing the technological complementarity of Asturian tools and whether such complementarity reflects deliberate technological choices. More broadly, this study shows that prehistoric tools were not necessarily formalized implements, and that materials often dismissed as “waste” by archaeologists, could have been recognized as tools by past humans.

Short-term prediction of avian hazard risk across airfields using machine learning and weather data
abstractText: This study employed three machine learning algorithms to address limitations in Next Generation Weather Radar (NEXRAD)-based bird activity risk forecasting by modeling eight weather features from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to predict Aircraft Hazard Advisory System (AHAS) risk categories up to three hours in advance. The prediction target was the AHAS NEXRAD-derived risk score provided by the Department of the Air Force Safety Center, which characterizes bird activity within radar sectors rather than observed bird-strike events. Long short-term memory recurrent neural network (LSTM-RNN), XGBoost, and Bayesian multinomial logistic regression (BMLR) models were evaluated across four US airfields. An ensemble of LSTM-RNN and XGBoost achieved the highest predictive accuracy, ranging from approximately 80% to 93% across the four airfields, with F1 scores of approximately 0.80. McNemar tests indicated statistically significant differences in classification performance among the evaluated models. The results demonstrate the feasibility of using weather-informed machine learning to extend AHAS risk prediction beyond contemporaneous NEXRAD observations and support multi-hour aviation risk assessment across geographically distinct airfields. Such forecasts could supplement existing bird-activity information during preflight planning and operational risk management. The full Python scripts, imputed datasets, and original AHAS risk data used in the analysis are archived in Zenodo (DOIs: 10.5281/zenodo.15760325, 10.5281/zenodo.22310818, and 10.5281/zenodo.22310839).

title: What drives social entrepreneurial intention? An integrated model of cognitive, moral, and social antecedents among university students in India
abstractText: Social entrepreneurship is pivotal in addressing social and environmental challenges, yet the psychological mechanisms underlying social entrepreneurial intention (SEI), especially in developing nations, remain underexplored. This study, grounded in the Theory of Planned Behaviour and the social entrepreneurial intention framework, investigates the cognitive, moral, normative, and experiential determinants of SEI among higher education students. Employing a quantitative methodology, a cross-sectional design was utilized, involving 349 postgraduate and undergraduate participants. The analysis was conducted using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that opportunity recognition competency (ORC) is the most significant predictor of SEI, underscoring the importance of entrepreneurial cognition in SEI. SEI is positively correlated with social entrepreneurial self-efficacy and subjective norms, indicating the significance of perceived entrepreneurial capability and social endorsement. However, SEI does not exhibit significant associations with empathy, moral obligation, perceived sustainability values, perceived social support, perceived behavioural control, or prior experience. Notably, prior experience is indirectly linked to SEI through social entrepreneurial self-efficacy, despite its direct and total associations with SEI being non-significant. Overall, the findings suggest that opportunity recognition competency, social entrepreneurial self-efficacy, and subjective norms hold greater relative importance for SEI when antecedents are evaluated concurrently.

title: The national sarcopenia atlas of China: geospatial patterns and region-specific cardiorenal risks among middle-aged and older adults
abstractText: Background Sarcopenia is a global challenge and a potential modifiable risk factor for cardiorenal diseases. However, the geospatial variation of sarcopenia in China and its region-specific associations with cardiovascular disease (CVD) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) remain poorly defined. Methods We analyzed participants aged over 45 years from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS, 2011–2020). Sarcopenia was defined by AWGS 2019 criteria. Spatial autocorrelation analysis (Moran's I) identified provincial clustering. Region-stratified longitudinal logistic regression assessed associations between baseline sarcopenia and incident CVD and CKD during a median 9.0-year follow-up. Results Among 12,263 participants (52.1% female; 27.4% aged over 65), spatial autocorrelation analysis identified significant 'High-High' sarcopenia clustering in Southwest China (P < 0.05), contrasting with 'Low-Low' clustering in Northern and Northeastern China (P < 0.05). In Southwest China, baseline sarcopenia was significantly associated with increased risk of incident CVD (OR 1.58, 95% CI 1.08–2.32, P < 0.05) and CKD (OR 1.76, 95% CI 1.17–2.63, P < 0.01). Notably, these longitudinal associations were not statistically significant in national-level analyses (CVD: OR 1.11, P = 0.40; CKD: OR 1.28, P = 0.09) or other regions. Conclusions This study provides the first national sarcopenia atlas for China, revealing significant geographic clustering and region-stratified associations with cardiorenal diseases. The increased risk specifically in Southwest China highlights the necessity for region-specific public health strategies and resource allocation for sarcopenia management.

title: From “KGeP” to the Protonated P4-like Anion (HGe3P)2– and the Endohedral Zintl Cluster [Mn@Ge10P2]3–
abstractText: P4-like Zintl anions (Tt2Pn2)2–, which combine the properties of the formally underlying homoatomic units, Tt44– or Pn4 (Tt = tetrel, group 14 element; Pn = pnictogen, group 15 element), are versatile starting materials for ternary clusters. However, not all of the theoretically possible Tt/Pn elemental combinations are accessible, and not all of them show decent reactivity. A particularly challenging elemental combination is that of Ge and P, in contrast to homoatomic P4 or Gen4– (n = 4, 9) that are widely used for corresponding reactions. The only report on a trinuclear complex, [Cd3(Ge3P)3]3–, obtained by reacting a “(Ge2P2)2–” anion, raised questions about the assumed 2:2 ratio of the atoms in the starting material. Herein, we aimed at clarifying the mystery about the composition and identifying a means of accessing new M/Ge/P-based cluster architectures. Regarding the first, we disclosed that the anion is actually not a 2:2 unit, but the first protonated version of a binary P4-like Zintl anion, (HGe3P)2–, which finally rationalizes the composition of the previously reported trinuclear complex. The anion was obtained as its [K(crypt-222)]+ salt by the extraction of “KGeP” with ethane-1,2-diamine (en), acting as a Brønsted acid toward the Zintl anion. 1H NMR spectroscopy and computations of NMR chemical shifts confirmed the presence of the protonated anion in the salt and in solution. As (HGe3P)2– did not show the desired reactivity, we used the more reductive extraction solution of “KGeP” in situ for a follow-up reaction with [Mn(Cp*)2], yielding the first Ge/P-based endohedral Zintl cluster, [Mn@Ge10P2]3–.

Proteome-wide identification of cysteine S-sulfenylation in response to low temperature and low-humidity stress in Dendrobium huoshanense
abstractText: Objective Dendrobium huoshanense is a renowned geo-authentic herb, and its excellent quality is closely correlated with the specific combined stress of low temperature and low humidity found in its native habitat. Methods In this study, we profiled the protein S-sulfenylation landscape of D. huoshanense under simulated low temperature and low humidity stress using Cys-Tag labeling coupled with Data-Independent Acquisition (DIA) mass spectrometry. Results Physiological analysis revealed a moderate accumulation of H₂O₂ at 12 h of stress, representing an early signaling phase. In total, 9,924 sulfenylation sites mapped to 6,953 proteins were identified. Following stress treatment, 226 sites showed differential modification, 202 of which were upregulated. Motif analysis demonstrated a significant enrichment of lysine and arginine residues flanking the modification sites. Functional enrichment analysis indicated that S-sulfenylation is primarily associated with vesicle trafficking, carbon metabolism, and amino acid biosynthesis. Conclusion This study characterizes the response of sulfenylated proteins to low temperature and low humidity stress in D. huoshanense , providing theoretical insights into the molecular mechanisms of plant redox regulation under abiotic stress.
