title: Linking Solvation Structure, Activity, and Electronic Structure to Electrochemical Stability in Lithium-ion Battery Electrolytes
abstractText: Electrolyte stability governs the performance and lifetime of Li-ion batteries, yet a quantitative molecular-level understanding of how salt concentration influences electrochemical stability remains elusive. Here, we combine molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, a lattice fluid theory, X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), density functional theory (DFT), and electrochemical measurements to quantitatively link solvation structure, thermodynamic activity, and electronic structure to the electrochemical stability of LiPF6 in EC/EMC (3:7 v/v) across a wide concentration range. We derive simple analytic expressions for species activities, parametrized using coordination numbers obtained from Raman spectroscopy, and validated against both MD simulations and experiment. Increasing salt concentration promotes PF6– participation in the Li+ solvation shell while suppressing free solvent populations, leading to systematic changes in the activities of species and an expanded electrochemical stability window. The lattice fluid theory directly links concentration-dependent solvation structure to measurable shifts in redox potentials via the Nernst equation, in good agreement with both computational predictions and experimental observations. DFT-predicted shifts in the unoccupied electronic states are confirmed by XAS measurements. These results establish a quantitative framework linking solvation structure, thermodynamic activity, and electronic structure to electrolyte stability, enabling the rational design of electrolytes with tailored electrochemical stability windows.

title: CEUS-guided hookwire localization combined with methylene blue staining for sentinel lymph node detection: a single-center clinical study
abstractText: Accurate identification of sentinel lymph nodes (SLNs) is essential for tumor staging and surgical decision-making. Although dye-guided SLN biopsy is widely used in clinical practice, relying on a single detection modality may lead to imprecise localization or missed detection of SLNs. Contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) has recently emerged as a promising imaging technique for visualizing lymphatic drainage and identifying SLNs. This study aimed to evaluate the complementary detection performance of CEUS-guided hookwire localization combined with methylene blue staining for SLN identification and to explore the potential predictive value of CEUS imaging grade for SLN metastasis. A total of 62 patients who underwent SLN biopsy were included in this single-arm clinical study. All patients underwent preoperative CEUS-guided hookwire localization followed by intraoperative methylene blue staining for SLN identification. The detection patterns of SLNs by CEUS and methylene blue were recorded and compared. In addition, CEUS imaging classified lymph nodes into three grades (I, II, and III), and the association between CEUS grade and pathological SLN metastasis was analyzed. SLNs were successfully identified in 60 of 62 patients, yielding an overall detection rate of 96.77%. A total of 222 sentinel lymph nodes were excised from 62 patients, with a mean of 3.63 nodes per patient.CEUS-guided hookwire localization and methylene blue staining demonstrated partial overlap in SLN identification. On a patient basis, 58 patients (93.54%) were identified by CEUS-guided hookwire localization, whereas 59 patients (95.16%) were identified by methylene blue staining, indicating complementary performance between the two techniques. Pathological examination revealed SLN metastasis in 6 patients (9.68%). All metastatic cases were detected by at least one of the two modalities. A trend toward increasing SLN positivity was observed across CEUS imaging grades (Grade I: 5.88%, Grade II: 11.54%, Grade III: 16.67% ). CEUS-guided hookwire localization combined with methylene blue staining demonstrates complementary value in SLN detection. CEUS imaging features show a trend toward higher SLN positivity; however, their predictive value for nodal metastasis remains exploratory and should be interpreted with caution.

title: The evolution and transmission dynamics of H3N2 influenza virus identified in a respiratory disease outbreak in companion dogs in Alabama, USA
abstractText: H3N2 Canine influenza virus (CIV)​, initially of avian origin, emerged in Asia around 2005–2007 and subsequently spread globally, reaching the USA in 2015. Despite initial containment efforts, H3N2 CIV re-emerged in several USA states in 2023. This study investigates the evolution and transmission dynamics of H3N2 CIV identified in companion dogs during an outbreak in Alabama, USA, between August and October 2022. We performed whole-genome sequencing on five H3N2 CIV isolates and conducted phylodynamic modeling, incorporating 100 global H3N2 CIV genomes per segment. Phylogenetic reconstruction showed the Alabama strains formed distinct, tightly clustered groups, suggesting recent common ancestry and localized evolution. Phylogeographic inference revealed discordant origins for different gene segments. The Hemagglutinin (HA), Matrix Protein (MP), Nucleoprotein (NP), Non-structural Protein (NS),​ and Polymerase Acidic (PA) genes traced ancestry to California strains, the Neuraminidase (NA) gene to Florida strains, and the Polymerase Basic1 (PB1) and Polymerase Basic2 (PB2) genes to Illinois strains. This genomic incongruence strongly indicates that the Alabama outbreak strain emerged through a reassortment event involving viruses from these three geographically distinct regions. The findings highlight reassortment as a mechanism driving H3N2 CIV evolution and spread, likely facilitated by the movement of infected dogs. Low vaccination coverage in dogs requires continued surveillance and shelter-focused vaccination to control CIV outbreaks and monitor adaptation.

title: Carexanes as Natural Ligands for a KRAS Promoter-Derived G-Quadruplex
abstractText: Natural products represent a valuable source of structurally diverse scaffolds for the development of ligands targeting noncanonical nucleic acid structures, such as G-quadruplex (GQ). Herein, we investigated the binding properties of four natural compounds extracted from Mediterranean plants─distachyasin, carexane B, carexane C, and magnoflorine─toward the GQ formed by the KRAS22-RT sequence, a modified KRAS-derived oligonucleotide commonly used as a model of the KRAS oncogene, which adopts a single, well-defined parallel intramolecular GQ structure. Circular dichroism (CD), UV/Vis, and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopies were employed to investigate the interactions between KRAS22-RT GQ and the four compounds. Among them, carexane B exhibited the strongest stabilizing effect on KRAS22-RT GQ. Moreover, it showed a preliminary binding preference for the KRAS22-RT GQ, with no appreciable spectroscopic perturbation detected under the experimental conditions employed with either the GQ derived from the C9orf72 gene (Orf72 GQ) or the model DNA duplex (ds12) obtained from the Dickerson dodecamer. Finally, the preliminary in vitro biological activity of the four compounds was assessed in three breast cancer cell lines.

title: Candidate gene discovery for rust resistance through multi-locus genome-wide association study in groundnut
abstractText: Rust, caused by Puccinia arachidis , is one among the most destructive fungal diseases constraining global groundnut ( Arachis hypogaea L.) production. While the development of disease-resistant varieties stands as the most effective approach to preventing substantial yield losses, the genetic mechanisms underlying resistance to rust is not yet well understood, emphasizing the necessity for further detailed research. In this study, 184 accessions from the ICRISAT groundnut mini-core collection were evaluated for rust resistance at Dharwad, India, across multiple seasons, as well as in Vietnam for one season. Whole-genome resequencing-based genome-wide association study (GWAS) identified five highly significant marker trait associations (MTAs) for rust resistance (p = 5.22 × 10 − 13 to 7.21 × 10 − 08 ). Among these, two robust rust-associated kompetitive allele specific PCR (KASP) markers, snpAH00607 at chromosome Ah01 and snpAH00609 at chromosome Ah17, were validated across diverse set of breeding and pre-breeding lines. These markers were linked to candidate genes encoding sterol C4-methyl oxidase 1–2 , implicated in brassinosteroid-mediated salicylic acid signalling, and MYB transcription factor known to be associated with defense responses. The identified SNPs, validated markers, and candidate genes will serve as important resources for marker-assisted breeding of rust disease resistant groundnut varieties.

title: Urea-carbon nanotube composites: Synthesis, characterization, and differential antibacterial activity against S. aureus and E. coli
abstractText: This study focuses on the synthesis, characterization, and antibacterial assessment of urea-functionalized carbon nanotube (CNT) composites. Amide nanotubes can be formed through the self-assembly of amphiphilic molecules driven by hydrogen-bonding interactions; however, previously reported approaches may be limited by aggregation and difficulties in large-scale production. In the present work, CNTs were functionalized with urea and systematically characterized using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), thermogravimetric analysis, scanning electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, and measurement of the zeta potential to evaluate their structural, chemical, thermal, morphological, and surface-charge properties. The results demonstrated the incorporation of urea-derived functionalities onto the CNT surface. Although functionalization decreased the thermal stability of the CNTs, the spectroscopic results indicated the presence of amide-related functional groups in the CNT–urea–CNT composite. Among the characterization techniques, XPS provided direct evidence of urea incorporation through the appearance of the N 1s signal and corresponding changes in the C 1s and O 1s spectra. Collectively, these results demonstrate substantial modification of the CNT surface following treatment with urea, without implying definitive covalent attachment. Measurement of the zeta potential further revealed a substantial alteration in the surface-charge behavior following functionalization. As pH increased, the zeta potential progressively decreased, a phenomenon that can be attributed to the deprotonation of surface functional groups. Pristine CNTs exhibited an isoelectric point (IEP) at approximately pH 7–8, whereas urea functionalization shifted the IEP to around pH 4, indicating a significant modification of the CNT surface chemistry. The urea–CNT and CNT–urea–CNT composites exhibited concentration-dependent antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli at 0.01–0.1 mg mL–1. The CNT–urea–CNT composite was more active against S. aureus at 0.05 and 0.1 mg mL–1, while the urea–CNT composite showed greater activity at 0.01 mg mL–1. The CNT–urea–CNT composite consistently exhibited stronger activity against E. coli, with a maximum inhibition zone of 33 ± 3.01 mm at 0.1 mg mL–1. These differences may reflect variations in surface structure, dispersion, and interactions with bacterial membranes.

Identity in the Age of AI: Toward a Functional Postphenomenology
abstractText: Advanced AI systems increasingly mediate the cognitive and practical functions through which personal identity is enacted: intention formation, deliberation, memory, self-expression, preference formation, and relational interaction. Drawing on Western and Confucian conceptions of identity, this paper advances a functional hypothesis specifying six domains in which AI may be reorganizing the conditions of agency, and outlines the implications for responsibility, consent, dignity, and institutional design. The argument is functional and normative rather than metaphysical: not that agency disappears, but that the architecture of the self that is presupposed by our normative categories may require renewed examination.

title: Assessing the interplay between yeast cell wall supplementation and oral Salmonella vaccines in poultry immunity
abstractText: Due to the increasing concerns over antibiotic-resistant bacterial strains, implementing alternative strategies has become crucial for poultry health. The use of Mannan-oligosaccharides (MOS) from Yeast cell wall (YCW), and the administration of oral vaccines, are strategies that can be leveraged to help reduce the incidence of Salmonella . When MOS enhances gut innate immunity, live attenuated Salmonella vaccines promote the development of a specific humoral response. However, studies have demonstrated the binding between MOS and Salmonella pathogenic strains, thereby raising questions about the effect of a YCW-supplemented diet on the live attenuated strains and the efficiency of these vaccines. Here, we show that despite this phenomenon, Salmonella vaccination is at least as effective among chickens fed with YCW as in the control group. No major differences were found in the circulating antibody titer, nor in the cytokines’ activation potential between the two groups. Furthermore, antigen-presenting cells’ class II major histocompatibility was overexpressed by 59.9%, and an increased frequency of 70.6% in mature B-cells among the treated animals was detected. Our results demonstrate that a YCW-supplemented diet has a time-specific but positive effect on the animal’s effective vaccine-induced protection. Therefore, even though binding between MOS and the vaccine may occur, it does not negatively impact the chicken’s immune protection.

title: Earthworm functional traits drive greenhouse gas emissions from casts through their effects on microbial and physicochemical properties
abstractText: ​Earthworms strongly influence soil biogeochemical processes, and cast formation may contribute to GHG emissions from soil. However, the main biotic and abiotic determinants of driving GHG emissions from earthworm casts and their links to earthworm functional traits remain poorly understood. This study investigated the effects of nine earthworm species across two contrasting soil types on CO2, N2O, and CH4 emissions from casts produced under controlled conditions. We hypothesized that these emissions are determined by specific earthworm traits influencing cast physicochemical properties and abundance of microbial functional groups. To this end, we measured 21 morpho-anatomical, physiological, and behavioral traits for each earthworm species and quantified GHG emissions and the abundance of microbial functional groups involved in GHG emissions in casts produced in Cambisol and Luvisol soils. Results showed that casts exhibited significantly higher GHG emissions, with CO2 increasing by up to 8-fold, N₂O by up to 7-fold, and CH₄ by up to 4-fold compared to control aggregates formed without earthworm activity. Emissions varied among species, with Lumbricus castaneus showing the highest CO4 (19-fold) and CH4 (11-fold) emissions, and Lumbricus terrestris the highest N2O emissions (22-fold). GHG emissions were strongly correlated with cast properties, including the abundances of total bacteria, ammonia oxidizers, and denitrifiers, as well as physicochemical parameters such as labile carbon pools (DOC and POM), mineral-associated organic matter (MAOM), nitrate availability, and moisture content. PLS-SEM analysis supported our hypothesis that earthworm traits, such as litter ingestion, body mass, mouth area, gizzard size, intestinal water content, and cast production, were indirectly influencing GHG emissions via modifications of cast properties (β = 0.88–0.92). Moreover, our findings indicated that the magnitude of GHG emissions from casts depended on soil type. These results suggest that soil management strategies favoring earthworm species with beneficial functional traits could help mitigate soil GHG emissions.

title: Model choice and prompt framing in LLM sustainability judgments
abstractText: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for sustainability assessment and decision support, yet their judgments may depend on the selected model and on how the task is defined. We compare 13 locally executed open-weight LLMs on 80 author-written sustainability scenarios using three prompt families that ask which actor should be responsible, bear the costs, or initiate action. Each model answered at two temperature settings with 100 repetitions, producing 624,000 deposited outputs, of which 610,708 contain a complete score vector. Scores were analyzed as relative actor support after removing each response’s overall level. Within this instrument, the cost prompt family produced the highest cross-model disagreement, exceeding both responsibility and catalyst by 7.37 points (question-cluster 95% intervals 5.56−9.15 and 5.38−9.36, describing variation across these 80 scenarios). It also produced the most lead-actor disagreement and the lowest full consensus. Moving from catalyst to cost reduced relative support for government and increased it for individuals and firms; moving from cost to responsibility largely reversed this pattern. These differences exceeded temperature-setting differences and persisted under model exclusion, alternative score transformations and tie rules, missing-response checks, and stems without explicit cost wording. Exploratory category patterns are conditional on uneven item coverage. Secondary rationale-language comparisons show the same within-model ordering but not the most cross-model variation under cost. Operational use should disclose model, prompt, and temperature choices; compare plausible alternatives; repeat generations; and refer high-disagreement judgments for human deliberation.

title: Motivators and Demotivators of Integrating Large Language Models in Software Engineering Education: An Exploratory Familiarity Allocation Framework
abstractText: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly influencing software engineering practice and education. However, limited research has examined their systematic integration using stakeholder evidence and quantitative decision-support models. This study presents an exploratory familiarity–allocation framework for analyzing motivating and demotivating factors associated with LLM integration in software engineering education. Building on our previously developed literature-based taxonomy, we evaluated 19 factors, comprising nine motivators and ten demotivators, through a structured survey of 126 stakeholders from multiple countries. Naive Bayes and Logistic Regression were used to examine associations between the factor ratings and high self-reported LLM familiarity. Both models achieved an accuracy of 0.461, below the majority-class baseline, indicating limited ability to distinguish respondents with higher and lower familiarity. Their estimated probabilities were therefore used as exploratory relative scoring functions rather than reliable individual-level predictions. These estimates were incorporated into a Genetic Algorithm using a defined allocation score to support Global Factor Allocation (GC), Local Factor Allocation (LC), and category-level \(\Delta\) Fitness analyses. The descriptive results identified Programming Assistance and Debugging Support , Personalized and Adaptive Learning , and AI as a Learning Partner as the most highly rated motivators. The most highly rated demotivators were Plagiarism and Intellectual Property Concerns , Over-Reliance on AI in Learning , and Reduced Critical Thinking and Problem-Solving . Under the fitted probability models and allocation assumptions, GC assigned relatively higher levels to integrity- and governance-related factors, while LC revealed additional pedagogical and risk-related patterns within individual categories. The resulting configurations represent exploratory familiarity–allocation scenarios rather than validated implementation priorities, institutional costs, or evidence of educational effectiveness. Classroom and institutional validation is required before the framework can guide LLM integration in practice.

title: The quality management system in medical laboratories: seventeen years of strengthening laboratory management towards ISO 15189 accreditation in Tanzania
abstractText: Background Recent advances in development and changes in laboratory technology seen in modern medicine have increased the demand on timely, accurate, reliable, and reproducible laboratory results. In public health settings, the laboratory plays a key role in disease surveillance for early detection and confirmation of disease outbreaks. We aimed to describe and document the 15189 accreditation in Tanzania. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study involving databases for medical laboratories in the Ministry of Health and African Society for Laboratory Medicine (ASLM). All laboratories which participated in quality management system in Tanzania were included in the study from national to health centre levels. Results Out of 157 laboratories implementing QMS from 2007 to 2024, a total of 81 (51.6%) laboratories were accredited. Secondary laboratory level had high number of enrolments into QMS program 117 (74.5%) followed by tertiary laboratories 26 (16.6%). The proportion of accredited laboratories at tertiary level was (73.1%) (p < 0.033) which was significantly higher compared to other levels. There was significantly higher proportion of laboratories accredited through direct laboratory accreditation process 25/28, (89.3%), compared with SLMTA program 59/129 (44.4%) (p < 0.001 ). There was a significant increase of accredited laboratories among SLMTA program from 1/76 (1.3%) in 2017 to 56/157 (35.7%) in 2024, ( p = 0.027) compared to direct laboratory accreditation approach. Conclusions Laboratory accreditation is a hallmark of quality management system implementation which can be achieved either through direct laboratory accreditation approach or the SLMTA program. The seventeen years of experience in implementing QMS indicates that the SLMTA program is more efficient, effectiveness and user-friendly than the direct laboratory accreditation approach.

title: Microplastics in edible aquatic species relevant to Europe: a systematic review and meta-analysis distinguishing chemically confirmed and apparent particles
abstractText: Microplastic measurements in edible aquatic species vary in chemical specificity, tissue, particle size and sampling unit, limiting comparisons and their interpretation as evidence of dietary exposure. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized occurrence and abundance in European production and consumption contexts. Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection were searched on 16 October 2026 for English-language articles indexed under bibliographic publication years 2020–2027. Two investigators independently assessed eligibility, verified extracted data and appraised methodological evidence. Chemically confirmed, apparent-only and inclusive evidence were synthesized separately, with confirmed occurrence requiring chemical identification linked to individual animals. Primary analyses required a supported maximum particle dimension no greater than 5 mm. Occurrence was synthesized using binomial–normal random-effects models; full-cohort abundance means greater than zero were synthesized on the logarithmic scale. The review included 361 reports, of which 149 contributed to at least one fitted analysis. Chemically confirmed gastrointestinal occurrence yielded a central study estimate of 30.6% (24 reports; 2,123 animals; 95% confidence interval [CI] 14.2–54.1%; 95% prediction interval 0.4–97.9%). Apparent-only gastrointestinal occurrence was 66.1% (38 reports; 95% CI 52.6–77.5%), while the overlapping inclusive estimate was 53.5% (62 reports). These estimates reflect different study sets and do not isolate the effects of identification methods. Confirmed gastrointestinal abundance yielded a geometric centre of report-level arithmetic means of 0.404 particles per animal in the analysed gastrointestinal material (13 reports; 95% CI 0.152–1.07). Estimates for muscle and edible bivalve soft tissues were sparse or imprecise. Pronounced heterogeneity, incomplete chemical coverage and limited biological replication constrain generalization across settings. Gastrointestinal findings cannot be directly translated into contamination of consumed portions, and the available evidence does not establish representative European prevalence or quantitative consumer-health risk. Measurements of consumed portions, with documented chemical identification and independent biological replication, are needed to strengthen dietary exposure assessment.

title: Integrating single‑cell transcriptomics and machine‑learning model screening to identify a KIAA0408‑associated B‑cell prognostic signature in ovarian cancer
abstractText: Ovarian cancer is the most lethal gynecologic malignancy, with most patients exhibiting suboptimal responses to T cell-targeted immune checkpoint inhibitors. Despite increasing attention to B cells in tumor immunity, the role of tumor-infiltrating B cells in ovarian cancer remains incompletely elucidated. Using single-cell RNA sequencing data, we constructed a high-resolution cellular atlas of the high-grade serous ovarian cancer, integrating inferCNV, CytoTRACE, and hdWGCNA to systematically analyze B cell copy number variations, differentiation trajectories, and co-expression networks. A machine learning-derived prognostic risk model was evaluated across multiple cohorts. The immune microenvironment was computationally profiled with ESTIMATE and immune deconvolution. KIAA0408‑related phenotypes were assessed by flow cytometry, immunoblotting, cell‑cycle, colony‑formation and CCK‑8 assays. Drug candidates were screened in databases and validated experimentally. Single-cell sequencing reveals ovarian cancer B cell heterogeneity, aberrant T-cell crosstalk, and KIAA0408 as a core regulator. The model of KIAA0408, CEACAM8, CAPZA1, PTCH1 and VPS13A showed prognostic stratification, pending validation in independent cohorts. High-risk patients exhibited an “ineffective inflammation” phenotype, featuring myeloid-derived suppressor cell-predominant infiltration, insufficient memory T cells, and impaired anti-tumor immunity. Mechanistically, KIAA0408 overexpression correlated with suppressed BCR‑AKT signaling and altered B‑cell‑cycle and conditioned‑medium phenotypes. Isoliquiritigenin showed antiproliferative effects, which may be linked to modulation of this pathway. This study reveals KIAA0408-mediated B-cell immune regulation in ovarian cancer, proposes a multi-gene prognostic model pending independent validation, and identifies isoliquiritigenin as a potential therapeutic agent.

title: Community-based health insurance and population health status in Rwanda, 2010–2025: trend, stationarity, regression and robustness analysis
abstractText: Rwanda’s Community-Based Health Insurance (CBHI; Mutuelles de Santé) is widely credited with advancing universal health coverage, but its population-level association with health outcomes has rarely been examined with explicit time-series methods. We assembled a national ecological annual dataset for 2010–2025 from Ministry of Health/RSSB reporting, World Bank World Development Indicators, and WHO/UN modelled estimates. Observed CBHI coverage (11 years) was the main explanatory variable; life expectancy, infant, under-five and maternal mortality, and out-of-pocket (OOP) expenditure were outcomes, with GDP per capita as control. We used Mann–Kendall and Sen’s slope trend tests, ADF and KPSS stationarity tests, OLS with Newey–West errors, variance inflation, Durbin–Watson and Breusch–Godfrey diagnostics, and first-differenced models. Life expectancy rose from 62.8 (2010) to 68.0 years (2024); infant and under-five mortality fell from 42.6 to 29.4 and from 63.3 to 37.7 per 1,000; OOP expenditure fell from 11.09% to 4.10% of current health expenditure (2023), a decline driven by the final observation. Outcome trends were monotonic (Mann–Kendall p < 0.001) and non-stationary in levels, whereas CBHI coverage (74.0–91.0%) showed no monotonic trend ( p = 0.81). Adjusting for GDP per capita, CBHI was not significantly associated with any outcome in levels ( p = 0.08–0.65) or first differences ( p = 0.21–0.92; six year-pairs). CBHI and GDP were not collinear (VIF ≤ 1.4). Autocorrelation-robust errors made the child-mortality coefficients nominally significant but in the unexpected direction, which we regard as a small-sample artefact. Rwanda’s health gains coincided with high CBHI coverage and economic growth, but eleven annual observations lack the power to isolate CBHI’s independent contribution. Harmonised annual and district-level CBHI data, and studies testing mediation through financial protection and utilisation, are needed.

title: Complete clip closure with staged triple-lumen feeding tube reduces delayed adverse events after duodenal endoscopic submucosal dissection
abstractText: BACKGROUND Given the thin duodenal wall and exposure of post-resection defects to bile and pancreatic juice, delayed adverse events (AEs) after duodenal endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) remain a major clinical challenge. While insufficient defect closure and suboptimal postoperative drainage have been implicated as potential risk factors, real-world evidence remains limited. We hypothesized that complete clip closure combined with structured postoperative management using a triple-lumen feeding tube would reduce delayed AEs by improving defect protection and reducing exposure to digestive secretions. AIM To explore the relationship between complete clip closure, a staged postoperative management protocol, and delayed AEs after duodenal ESD. METHODS We retrospectively analyzed 179 consecutive patients who underwent duodenal ESD. The patients’ baseline characteristics were compared according to delayed AE occurrence. Independent risk factors for postoperative complications were identified through univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses. Clip closure quality (complete vs incomplete) and postoperative management strategy (triple-lumen feeding tube vs nasogastric tube) effects on clinical outcomes were evaluated through subgroup analyses. The relationship between drainage strategy and perioperative inflammatory markers and nutritional indicators was examined through covariance analyses. RESULTS Delayed AEs occurred in 12.8% of patients. Multivariable analysis demonstrated that complete clip closure [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 0.16, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.12-0.22; P < 0.001] and postoperative triple-lumen feeding tube placement (aOR = 0.64, 95%CI: 0.46-0.87; P < 0.001) were independently associated with lower delayed AEs risk. Patients who received complete closure and triple-lumen feeding tube drainage had the lowest observed incidence there of (2.8%). On postoperative day 1, the triple-lumen feeding tube group had a significantly lower neutrophil percentage than the nasogastric tube group [model 2: Adjusted mean difference (AMD) = -1.82], whereas serum albumin (model 2: AMD = 0.41) and total protein levels (model 2: AMD = 0.85) were significantly higher (all P < 0.05). CONCLUSION Complete clip closure and postoperative triple-lumen feeding tube management were independently associated with fewer delayed AEs after duodenal ESD.

title: Candidate gene polymorphisms, MHC-linked markers, genome-wide loci and host-gene manipulation in relation to Newcastle disease outcomes in chickens: a systematic review
abstractText: Background Newcastle disease (ND), caused by avian orthoavulavirus 1, remains a major constraint on chicken production. This review evaluated evidence linking host genetic variants and experimental manipulation of named host genes to Newcastle disease virus (NDV) outcomes in chickens. Methods Following PRISMA 2020, Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed were searched from January 2000 to October 2026, and records from preliminary searches were added. Eligible studies genotyped host variation, or knocked out, substituted, or overexpressed a named host gene, in chickens or chicken cells and measured an NDV-specific outcome. Methodological quality was appraised across ten domains, and results were synthesised narratively by gene category and NDV exposure protocol. Results From 1315 screened database records and 139 other records, 56 reports of 49 studies were included: 14 on major histocompatibility complex (MHC)-linked markers, three on Mx association, eight on other candidate genes, 14 genome-wide or quantitative trait locus studies and 17 functional studies. Twenty-three reports used vaccination only, 13 in vivo challenge or natural exposure, and 17 in vitro infection. Robustness was high in eight reports, moderate in 21 and low in 27. MHC-linked variation was associated with vaccine-induced antibody or T-cell responses in 11 reports, but favourable alleles differed between populations; the only variance-component estimate attributed 2.3% of phenotypic variance to the MHC, and no association was found with embryo survival or viral load. Evidence for natural Mx variation was limited and inconsistent, whereas Mx knockout increased NDV replication in chicken cells. Heritabilities were low to moderate, most loci were suggestive, and a chromosome 24 region was associated with viral load in two independent challenged populations. Functional studies showed that interferon pathway genes, including IFIT5, IFNAR1, and TRIM25 , restrict NDV in chicken cells. Conclusions Host genetic variation influences NDV-related responses, but no single marker is ready for selection. MHC-linked associations are repeatable mainly for vaccine-induced immune responses and are population-specific; evidence for Mx polymorphisms is weak, and genome-wide results indicate a polygenic architecture. Genomic selection in phenotyped reference populations under standardised challenge protocols is the most promising route.

title: Endoscopic diagnosis and treatment of early gastric cardia neoplasms: Efficacy and management of non-curative resection
abstractText: BACKGROUND Gastric cardia cancer is a distinct clinicopathological entity with an increasing global incidence. Because of its location at the esophagogastric junction and complex submucosal architecture, early gastric cardia neoplasms pose significant challenges for accurate endoscopic diagnosis and depth assessment. These difficulties may lead to pathological underestimation and high rates of noncurative resection (NCR) after endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD). Although additional surgery is generally recommended for NCR, this strategy may lead to overtreatment in selected low-risk patients. Therefore, evaluating the diagnostic performance of endoscopic modalities and exploring individualized management strategies after ESD are important clinically. AIM To evaluate ESD efficacy and safety for early gastric cardia neoplasms and explore individualized management for patients undergoing NCR. METHODS We retrospectively analyzed 155 patients with 163 early gastric cardia mucosal lesions treated by ESD between March 2014 and June 2025. Diagnostic accuracy of white-light endoscopy, magnifying endoscopy with narrow-band imaging, and endoscopic ultrasonography was evaluated using postoperative pathology as the reference standard. ESD outcomes, management of NCR, and long-term survival were assessed. Logistic regression identified factors associated with NCR, and survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox models. RESULTS Most lesions were classified as E = G type (Nishi classification) and located on the posterior wall of the cardia. White-light endoscopy showed a diagnostic accuracy of 70.6% (κ = 0.21), compared with 84.3% (κ = 0.54) for magnifying endoscopy with narrow-band imaging. Endoscopic ultrasonography demonstrated an accuracy of 69.5% (κ = 0.12) for assessing invasion depth. All lesions were removed en bloc ; histologically complete resection was achieved in 82.8% of cases, and 73.0% met the e-Cura criteria for curative resection. Complications were rare (bleeding 1.8%). The 5-year overall survival and disease-free survival rates were 97.0% and 94.5%, respectively. Of the 44 patients with NCR (27.0%), 7 underwent additional surgery (with no residual tumor or nodal metastasis found) and 37 opted for surveillance. The 5-year disease-free survival was 85.7% in the surgery group and 93.5% in the surveillance group. CONCLUSION ESD is effective for early gastric cardia neoplasms. Individualized surveillance for low-risk NCR patients helps reduce overtreatment and improve clinical prognosis.

title: Influence of pregnancy on outcomes of inflammatory bowel disease and treatment discontinuation
abstractText: BACKGROUND Treatment of inflammatory bowel diseases (IBDs) is challenging due to the maintenance of remission and associated fetal safety concerns during pregnancy. While existing literature emphasizes the importance of achieving remission prior to conception, optimal management of IBD during pregnancy remains underexplored, especially regarding medication continuation and efficacy. AIM To evaluate the effect of treatment discontinuation on disease activation and pregnancy outcomes in a cohort of patients with IBD. METHODS This observational study was performed with pregnant patients with IBD between March 2019 and June 2023. Clinical features, treatment details, disease activation and outcomes were collected and analyzed. RESULTS A total of 57 pregnant woman was included, of whom 37 (64.9%) had ulcerative colitis (UC) while 20 (35.1%) had Crohn’s disease (CD). Before pregnancy, medical treatments for UC patients included mesalazine in 29 (78.4%) patients, thiopurine in 20 (54.1%) and biologic therapy in 6 (16.2%). Among the CD patients, 13 (65%) received biologic therapy and 7 (35%) received thiopurine. The most commonly prescribed biologic agent was infliximab for both diseases. During pregnancy, 16 (28.1%) patients, including 6 (18.8%) with UC and 10 (50%) with CD, had a history of treatment discontinuation. Thirteen (81%) medications were discontinued in line with the patient’s preference, with the vast majority of these discontinuations occurring immediately after confirmation of pregnancy rather than during the preconception planning phase. Notably, the majority of cases of patients discontinuing their treatment independently occurred prior to any structured medical counseling regarding the safety of IBD medications during pregnancy. Disease activation occurred for 25 (43.9%) patients, including 10 (50%) with CD and 15 (40.5%) with UC. Twelve (48%) patients required steroids due to activation. There were 54 (94.7%) live births and no statistically significant difference in the live birth rate according to whether disease activation developed or not [23 (92%) vs 31 (96.9%), P = 0.576]. The abortion rate was not associated with disease activation (P > 0.05). No serious infections occurred in the first month following birth. CONCLUSION The discontinuation of medical treatment during pregnancy at the patient’s discretion was significantly correlated with disease exacerbations, particularly in patients with UC, and subsequent salvage steroid treatment. These findings underscore the vital role of patient counseling prior to and during pregnancy, with the objective of ensuring medication compliance and optimizing maternal and fetal outcomes.

title: Divergent antiviral function of Atlantic salmon trim25 paralogues in infectious salmon anaemia virus infection
abstractText: Background Aquaculture production of Atlantic salmon is a rapidly growing food sector, offering numerous advantages over terrestrial livestock. However, infectious diseases remain a major constraint, reducing production efficiency and compromising fish health and welfare. Developing improved preventative and therapeutic strategies requires a deeper understanding of the host immune response. In model species, the E3 ubiquitin ligase TRIM25 is a well-characterised regulator of antiviral immunity, functioning as both a sensor and signal transducer within the RIG-I-like receptor pathway. In Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar ), trim25 exists as two paralogues located on chromosomes 2 and 12 and has been identified as a virus-induced gene during multiple viral infections. However, its antiviral role remains poorly understood. This research aimed to characterise the function of trim25 to improve our understanding of antiviral immunity and inform strategies for managing viral diseases in salmon aquaculture. Results Using Atlantic salmon head kidney (SHK-1) cells infected with infectious salmon anaemia virus (ISAV), we identified paralogue-specific virus inducibility and antiviral activity. Although structural analyses showed both paralogues retained conserved functional domains, genome editing, qPCR, and epigenetic sequencing demonstrated that only the chromosome 2 paralogue (Ssa02 trim25 ) significantly influenced viral replication. RNA sequencing further demonstrated conservation of TRIM25 function within the RIG-I-like receptor signalling pathway. Finally, overexpression of trim25 enhanced protection against ISAV infection. Conclusions These findings identify a paralogue-specific antiviral role for trim25 in Atlantic salmon and provide new insights into the evolution of antiviral immunity following genome duplication. They also highlight trim25 as a promising target for future biotechnological approaches to improve disease resistance and reduce the impact of viral outbreaks in salmon aquaculture.

title: Instrumental convergence and power seeking
abstractText: Recent years have seen increasing concern that artificial intelligence may soon pose an existential risk to humanity. One leading ground for concern is that artificial agents may be power-seeking, aiming to acquire power and in the process disempowering humanity. I show how the argument from power-seeking rests on a strong version of a claim known as the instrumental convergence thesis. I explore leading defenses of the instrumental convergence thesis and argue that none establishes the thesis in a strong enough form to ground the argument from power-seeking. I discuss implications for longtermism, the governance of artificial intelligence, and the methodology of studying risks posed by artificial agents.

title: Inflammation and Late-Life Depressive Symptoms: Inflammation et symptômes dépressifs chez les personnes âgées
abstractText: Background Low-level systemic inflammation has been associated with late-life depressive symptoms. Whether individuals with higher inflammation derive preventive benefit from low-dose aspirin therapy is unknown. Methods We performed a post-hoc analysis of the ASPirin in Reducing Events in the Elderly (ASPREE) randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. Baseline high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) was measured in plasma and depressive symptoms were assessed annually using the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression 10 Scale (CES-D-10), with elevated symptoms defined as CES-D-10 ≥ 8. Participants with elevated depressive symptoms at baseline were excluded. We fitted population-averaged logistic generalized estimating equation models adjusted for baseline sociodemographic and lifestyle covariates, including an hsCRP × treatment interaction to test effect modification by aspirin. Results Higher baseline hsCRP was associated with increased odds of elevated depressive symptoms during follow-up (OR 1.07 per SD increase in hsCRP, 95% CI 1.03–1.11). Low-dose aspirin allocation did not modify the hsCRP-depressive symptoms association (interaction OR 1.02, 95% CI 0.94–1.10). Findings were similar after additional adjustment for comorbidity and other covariates. Conclusions In community-dwelling older adults during the ASPREE randomized trial period, higher baseline hsCRP was modestly associated with elevated depressive symptoms. There was no evidence that low-dose aspirin was associated with reduced risk of depressive symptoms among participants with higher baseline inflammation.

title: Nitrogen fertilisation reveals contrasting nitrogen-use efficiency and greenhouse gas emission intensity responses in linseed and oilseed rape
abstractText: Break crops vary in nitrogen (N) demand, yet direct comparisons of their nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) and greenhouse gas (GHG) emission intensity are limited. We compared four linseed ( Linum usitatissimum ) genotypes with one oilseed rape (OSR; Brassica napus ) genotype in a controlled glasshouse experiment across four N fertiliser rates (0–120 kg N ha − 1 ). Plant growth traits, NUE, daily and cumulative GHG fluxes (N 2 O, CO 2 , CH 4 ) and emission intensity (kg CO 2 e kg − 1 biomass) were quantified. OSR produced greater biomass, chlorophyll content, and NUE than linseed at all N rates. Absolute GHG emissions rose more steeply with increasing fertiliser in OSR. Consequently, CO 2 e emission intensity increased with N rate in linseed but decreased in OSR, consistent with biomass dilution. Fertiliser rate was the dominant driver of GHG fluxes; crop type had no independent effect on cumulative emissions once N rate was accounted for. Genotypic variation within linseed was negligible compared with crop- and fertiliser-driven effects. These results highlight a yield-emission trade-off: OSR maximises productivity but requires careful N management to control emissions while linseed maintains lower emission intensity under reduced N inputs. Linseed offers potential as a lower-intensity break crop in diversified, low-N rotations. Further field-scale evaluation needed to support agricultural decarbonisation.

title: A novel optical scanning system for laser machining of vertical sidewall
abstractText: Despite its many advantages, laser micromachining has limitations, such as tapering due to plasma-induced distortion, gaussian beam profiles, and defocusing effects. Although process parameter optimization and adjusting the angle-of-incidence (AOI) have been investigated to reduce tape angle of the sidewall, existing approaches often require complex process optimization, workpiece tilting, or multi-axis scanning systems. In this study, we developed a novel optical scanning system consisting of three spherical lenses and a 2D galvanometer scanner to enable AOI variation using a simplified optical configuration. To overcome the tapering limitations of machined surfaces, this study developed a novel optical scanning system and proposed a derived machining process. The proposed optical scanning system controls the AOI of the laser beam on the sample surface through a novel arrangement of spherical lenses. The experimentally measured AOI showed good agreement with the optical simulation, confirming the validity of the proposed optical system. Under optimized machining conditions of a fluence of 2.97 J/cm 2 , an overlap ratio of 10 %, and a scan number of 100, a near-vertical sidewall with a taper angle of 0.7° was achieved at an AOI of 4.058°. Furthermore, we observed that the taper angle during machining was highly sensitive to the AOI. The proposed method has the potential to limit the formation of taper angles in conventional laser machining and enhance industrial applicability through an optical design-based AOI control system.

title: Optimal 10-mm window: Integrating peri-ablation radiomics with preoperative features to predict early hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence after thermal ablation
abstractText: BACKGROUND Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a global health challenge. Thermal ablation (TA) is a guideline-recommended curative treatment for early-stage HCC. Early recurrence after TA, often arising from occult metastases missed during initial staging, is associated with a poorer prognosis. In this context, noninvasive imaging plays a critical role in assessing treatment response and stratifying recurrence risk in HCC. AIM To develop and validate a radiomics model integrating pre- and post-ablation features for predicting early HCC recurrence after TA. METHODS This retrospective study enrolled 301 patients who underwent initial TA for HCC and divided them into training (n = 168), internal validation (n = 72), and external validation (n = 61) sets. Radiomic features were extracted from pre-operative ultrasound and contrast-enhanced ultrasound images of the tumor, as well as from postoperative contrast-enhanced ultrasound images of four peri-ablation margins (5-20 mm from the ablation zone). Seven classifiers integrating clinical, pre-operative radiomic, and margin features were developed. Model performance was assessed using area under the curve (AUC), calibration, and decision curve analysis, followed by SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis. RESULTS A total of 301 patients, including 109 with ER, were included. The baseline model, based solely on pre-operative clinical and radiomic features, yielded an AUC of 0.849. Integration of features from concentric peri-ablation zones showed that model improvement depended on the spatial extent of the analyzed region. The optimal 10-mm peri-ablation support vector machine (SVM) model achieved the highest test-set AUC of 0.876 (95% confidence interval: 0.784-0.969), significantly outperforming the preoperative-only baseline model (AUC = 0.849). Models incorporating the 5-mm (AUC = 0.863) and 15-mm (AUC = 0.863) margins showed similar, though slightly lower, performance, whereas extending the analysis to a 20-mm margin resulted in a marked decline in performance (AUC = 0.795). SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified five top predictive radiomic features derived from pre-operative multiphase and postoperative portal-phase images. CONCLUSION Integrating pre-operative ultrasound with 10-mm peri-ablation radiomics effectively predicts early HCC recurrence after TA and may serve as a potential biomarker for risk stratification.

title: Crosstalk between neutrophils and hepatic stellate cells in liver injury and repair: Mechanisms and implications
abstractText: The liver has a remarkable capacity for regeneration; however, persistent or dysregulated inflammation can impair tissue repair, thereby promoting chronic fibrosis and, ultimately, cirrhosis. Neutrophils and hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) are key mediators of this pathological transition. Beyond the traditional view of neutrophils as short-lived effectors of tissue injury, accumulating evidence indicates that they exhibit marked plasticity and can adopt either pro-inflammatory or pro-repair phenotypes depending on the microenvironment. Recent studies have revealed a dynamic and bidirectional communication network between neutrophils and HSCs that regulates injury severity, resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and fibrotic progression. This review summarizes the mechanistic evidence for neutrophils-HSCs crosstalk, with a focus on the following aspects: (1) Initiating soluble mediators, including reactive oxygen species, proteases, and cytokines; (2) Signal amplification through extracellular matrix remodeling and mechanotransduction; and (3) The role of neutrophil extracellular traps as a signaling platform that sustains profibrotic programs. In addition, the review highlights how temporal factors and disease context determine whether this crosstalk facilitates regenerative repair or evolves into a self-amplifying fibrotic circuit. Finally, translational opportunities are discussed, and it is proposed that next-generation antifibrotic strategies should prioritize phase-specific and precision-based remodeling of key regulatory nodes.

title: GA-VINO: A Geometry-Aware Variational Physics-Informed Neural Operator for Mindlin–Reissner Plates
abstractText: Plate and shell structures are widely used in engineering fields. Rapid response prediction for such structures under complex geometries, heterogeneous materials, and varying loads is important for engineering design, but conventional numerical methods usually require repeated modeling and solution when the physical configuration changes. To address this issue, this study proposes a geometry-aware variational physics-informed neural operator (GA-VINO) for Mindlin–Reissner plates. GA-VINO represents the plate geometry using boundary point clouds and incorporates a material encoder, a load encoder, and a scalar-parameter branch to handle spatially random material fields, spatially varying loads, and sample-level uniform parameters. Through multi-branch point cloud encoding and cross-attention, GA-VINO fuses geometric, material, loading, and query point information, and predicts the transverse deflection and rotations at arbitrary query locations. Unlike conventional data-driven neural operators, GA-VINO requires no labeled solution data during training. Instead, it minimizes a variational physics-informed loss constructed from the discretized total potential energy of the Mindlin–Reissner plate. Compared with grid-based neural operators, GA-VINO directly processes irregular point clouds and allows different physical fields to be discretized on different point sets, avoiding forced interpolation onto a common grid. Numerical results demonstrate that GA-VINO achieves accurate predictions across varying geometries, material properties, and loading conditions, with lower H 1 seminorm and energy-norm errors and more accurate predictions of bending moments and transverse shear forces than data-driven baselines. Furthermore, GA-VINO enables millisecond-level full-field inference and demonstrates useful generalization capability under moderate geometric distribution shifts, although its prediction accuracy decreases under stronger geometric extrapolation.

title: Bridge of imbalance: How does the brain-gut axis act as a catalyst for gastrointestinal tumors in aging
abstractText: Aging is a complex biological process regulated by multiple factors. Its characteristics include shortening of telomere length, DNA damage, abnormal secretion of cytokines, and cellular oxidative damage. These changes eventually lead to the formation of tumor cells and the remodeling of the intestinal microenvironment. The brain-gut axis is a complex bidirectional communication network connecting the intestine and the central nervous system, composed of the nervous system, immune system, microbiota and their metabolites. It allows for information exchange between the intestine and the brain, influencing the function of the digestive system and brain activity. The remodeling of the brain-gut axis function caused by aging is an important catalyst promoting the development of gastrointestinal tumors. In aging, the dysbiosis of the intestinal microbiota, abnormal release of neurotransmitters, and neuroendocrine disorders will directly affect tumor occurrence through the brain-gut axis. In addition, aging can put the gastrointestinal tract in an inflammaging state, causing dysregulation of cancer immune. At the same time, the disruption of the circadian rhythm can affect the homeostasis of the gastrointestinal tract and promote tumor development. This review will specifically explore the factors that induce gastrointestinal tumors in aging through the components of the brain-gut axis and propose new therapeutic perspectives targeting the intestinal microbiota, neurotransmitters, immune conditions, and clock rhythm.

title: EIF5B /mitogen-activated protein kinase 1 axis drives tumor progression and confers dual resistance to chemotherapy and immunotherapy in colonic adenocarcinoma
abstractText: BACKGROUND Although eukaryotic translation initiation factor 5B (EIF5B ) is implicated in the pathogenesis of multiple malignancies, its functional impact in colonic adenocarcinoma (COAD) is still not well defined. AIM To determine EIF5B ’s role, mechanisms, and therapeutic associations in COAD. METHODS To assess the prognostic value of EIF5B , we integrated pan-cancer bioinformatic screening with clinical validation in COAD cohorts. The oncogenic function and molecular regulations were evaluated through in vitro and in vivo assays, multi-omic pathway enrichment, Western blotting, rescue experiments, immune infiltration and drug-sensitivity modeling. RESULTS Our results showed significant overexpression of EIF5B in COAD tissues, and its correlation with unfavorable patient outcomes. Functional analysis revealed that EIF5B induced migration, proliferation, and invasion in vitro , as well as promoted tumorigenesis in vivo through phosphorylation of mitogen-activated protein kinase 1 (MAPK1). In addition, the immune microenvironment exhibited a suppressed phenotype, accompanied by decreased predictive scores for programmed cell death protein 1/cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated antigen-4 blockade and reduced predicted sensitivity to chemotherapeutic agents. EIF5B expression, immune evasion, and drug sensitivity were associated with the MAPK signaling pathway. CONCLUSION EIF5B mediated phosphorylation of MAPK1 regulates the progression of COAD, suggesting EIF5B as potential therapeutic target for overcoming resistance against chemotherapy and immunotherapy.

title: Changes in liver and spleen stiffness after transarterial chemoembolization for hepatocellular carcinoma and role in predicting hepatic decompensation
abstractText: BACKGROUND Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) alters hepatic perfusion and can potentially impact portal pressure in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients. Liver stiffness measurements (LSM) and spleen stiffness measurements (SSM) have emerged as promising tools for assessing portal hypertension. However, limited data exist regarding the effects of TACE on LSM and SSM. We hypothesized that TACE may influence short-term LSM and SSM and that baseline stiffness values can effectively identify patients at high risk for postprocedural hepatic decompensation. AIM To evaluate the short-term effects of TACE on stiffness measurements, and assess their baseline values for predicting 6-month hepatic decompensation. METHODS This prospective cohort study enrolled 102 HCC patients undergoing TACE. LSM and SSM measured by elastography at baseline, day 10, and day 30 post-procedure. A linear mixed-effects model was used to account for missing data with time as a fixed effect and participant identification as a random effect. Hepatic decompensation was defined as a composite endpoint of ascites, variceal bleeding, overt hepatic encephalopathy, and severe liver injury. Multiple logistic regression identified independent predictors of 6-month hepatic decompensation. RESULTS The linear mixed-effects model revealed no significant change in LSM and SSM values on days 10 and 30 after TACE compared to baseline. Within 6 months, 19 patients (18.6%) developed hepatic decompensation. Baseline SSM > 54 kilopascals (kPa) predicted hepatic decompensation with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.83 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.72-0.93], sensitivity of 63.2%, specificity of 90.4%. Multivariate analysis identified modified albumin-bilirubin (mALBI) grade ≥ 2B [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 7.05, 95%CI: 1.92-25.94, P = 0.003] and baseline SSM > 54 kPa (aOR = 16.52, 95%CI: 4.39-62.19, P < 0.001) as independent predictors of decompensation. CONCLUSION TACE does not significantly affect short-term stiffness measurements. However, baseline SSM can serve as an effective surrogate marker that complements the mALBI grade for stratifying hepatic decompensation risk.

title: Study on the adhesive effect of deoxyshikonin on Helicobacter pylori
abstractText: BACKGROUND Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori ) infection remains a major etiological factor in chronic gastritis, peptic ulcer disease, and gastric cancer. The increasing prevalence of antibiotic resistance underscores the urgent need for alternative anti-H. pylori agents with clearly characterised molecular targets. AIM To investigate whether deoxyshikonin inhibits H. pylori adhesion by modulating urease-associated pathways. METHODS Anti-adhesion activity of deoxyshikonin was evaluated in GES-1 and BGC823 cells using Gram staining, fluorescence microscopy, the Alamar Blue Assay, and colony counting. Potential targets were identified using drug affinity-responsive target stability-mass spectrometry and molecular docking. Urease involvement was investigated using reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction, western blotting, surface plasmon resonance, phenol red colorimetry, and urease activity assays. A low-urease-expression 26695Δcfa mutant and exogenous urease supplementation were applied for mechanistic validation. RESULTS Deoxyshikonin reduced cell-associated H. pylori in a concentration-dependent manner. Molecular docking suggested a stronger binding of deoxyshikonin to UreB than to UreA (-6.1 kcal/mol vs -4.9 kcal/mol). Deoxyshikonin downregulated ureA /ureB and SabA /BabA transcripts; reduced UreB protein abundance; inhibited urease activity; and directly bound to UreB , as demonstrated by surface plasmon resonance analysis (KD = 1.193 μM). The H. pylori 26695Δcfa mutant was less susceptible to deoxyshikonin, whereas exogenous urease promoted bacterial adhesion. CONCLUSION Deoxyshikonin inhibits H. pylori adhesion. The current evidence indicates that the urease subunits UreA and UreB are involved as molecular targets in this effect.

title: A complete-coverage path-planning algorithm based on local path cost
abstractText: Complete coverage path planning (CCPP) is a core enabling technology for autonomous operation and navigation of mobile robots and unmanned surface vehicles (USVs). However, in large-scale and complex environments, due to the lack of directional guidance in population evolution, existing heuristic path planners often suffer from slow convergence, premature trapping in local optima, and excessive turning maneuvers along the planned tour. To mitigate the blindness of conventional mutation operators, this paper proposes a complete-coverage path-planning algorithm based on local path cost (CCPP-LPC). First, a local path cost evaluation model is constructed to adaptively quantify the possible impact that each node may have on the overall path length, thereby identifying nodes with high optimization potential. Second, an adaptive dual-guided perturbation node selection strategy is designed, which derives both optimization-oriented and diversity-oriented probability distributions from local costs, guiding the population to preferentially refine high-cost segments while preserving gene diversity. To assess the performance of CCPP-LPC, comprehensive comparisons against six state-of-the-art heuristic algorithms on four simulated grid maps of varying scales and complexity are conducted, as well as four simulation maps from real environment. Experimental results show that CCPP-LPC not only improves computational efficiency, but also achieves the best performance across key metrics, including path length, and repeated coverage ratio. These outcomes highlight CCPP-LPC as a practically valuable approach for complete-coverage optimization under multi-constrained, complex environments.

title: Mitigation of Cd Accumulation in Rice by the Combination of Mg-modified Biochar/attapulgite Materials and Foliar Inhibitors
abstractText: Cadmium (Cd) is a highly toxic heavy metal that poses serious threats to both human health and plant growth. It exhibits several environmental risks, including high enrichment potential, mobility, chemical stability, long persistence in soil, and resistance to microbial degradation. In this study, a novel Mg-modified biochar/palygorskite composite material was developed and applied in field experiments to evaluate its effects on soil pH, organic matter content, as well as the speciation and concentration of Cd. Furthermore, the effectiveness of integrating foliar control techniques in mitigating Cd accumulation across various rice tissues was investigated. The experimental results demonstrated MgCl₂/BA and MgO/BA increased soil pH by 0.46 and 0.53 units, respectively, resulting in a 41.02% and 38.83% increase in soil organic matter content. At the same time, the available Cd content in the soil significantly decreased, as the acid-soluble and reducible fractions of Cd were transformed into oxidizable and residual forms. Besides, Cd content in rice grains treated with MgCl₂/BA and MgO/BA decreased by 66.22% and 72.90% respectively. After the foliar application of the remediation agent, the Cd content in rice grains further decreased by 20.54% and 13.22% respectively. Moreover, the application of the remediation agent contributed to an increase in rice yield.

Evaluation of an innovative outpatient palliative care model for patients with advanced cancer: a multicenter randomized clinical trial
abstractText: As European healthcare increasingly relies on outpatient services, including palliative care, additional ambulatory options are needed to meet demand. The rising complexity and scope of patients’ palliative care needs call for new outpatient tools. Our study evaluates the impact of an innovative palliative care clinic on health status in adults with advanced cancer. A superiority multicenter randomized clinical trial comparing an innovative palliative care day hospital (intervention arm) with traditional outpatient palliative care clinics (standard arm) over a six month-period. Adults with solid tumors newly referred to outpatient palliative care at six centers were enrolled, with the option to nominate a primary caregiver for caregiver needs assessment. The primary outcome was health-related quality-of-life deterioration–free survival, assessed using the EORTC Core Quality of Life questionnaire (QLQ-C30). Secondary outcomes included anxiety and depression symptoms, satisfaction with care, indicators of aggressive end-of-life care, overall survival, and caregivers’ supportive care needs among those with an identified primary caregiver. Exploratory outcomes included advance care planning discussions and patients’ perceptions of prognosis and treatment goals. Among 139 participants (mean age 67 years; 70% female; 31% breast cancer) randomized to the intervention (n = 70) or standard arm (n = 69), 34 (48.7%) and 33 (47.1%), respectively, designated a caregiver. The primary outcome was negative (p > 0.05). Over time, secondary endpoints showed a significant decrease in depression scores in the interventional arm (mean difference: − 2.30; 95% CI: − 4.57 to − 0.04; p = 0.046), while the standard arm had significantly lower psychological/emotional needs (mean difference: 0.50; 95% CI: 0.15–0.99; p = 0.044) and communication/family support needs (mean difference: 0.27; 95% CI: 0.01–0.52; p = 0.043). No significant differences were found in satisfaction with care, supportive care needs, aggressive end-of-life care, advance care planning, prognosis perception, or overall survival. Access to a palliative care day hospital did not improve HRQoL deterioration-free survival or most secondary outcomes versus traditional outpatient palliative care. Its role may therefore be best targeted to patients with particularly complex or high-intensity palliative care needs. NCT04604873 in the registry IDRCB 2019-A03116–51. title: Effects of berberine-containing vs clarithromycin-containing quadruple therapy on intestinal microbiota during Helicobacter pylori eradication
abstractText: BACKGROUND Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori ) eradication is crucial for managing H. pylori -related gastrointestinal diseases. Berberine, a natural alkaloid, has shown potential anti-H. pylori activity, but its effectiveness and feasibility remain unclear. AIM To evaluate the H. pylori eradication efficacy of berberine and its impact on intestinal flora, compared with clarithromycin-based therapy. METHODS A total of 41 subjects with positive 13C-urea breath test were randomly divided into group A (berberine group) and group B (clarithromycin group). All participants underwent 14-day quadruple therapy with omeprazole 20 mg once daily, amoxicillin 0.5 g three times daily and bismuth potassium citrate 1 g four times daily; group A substituted berberine 0.3 g three times daily, whereas group B substituted berberine with clarithromycin 0.5 g twice daily. Fecal samples were collected before (A1, B1) and after (A2, B2) treatment for 16S rRNA gene sequencing to analyze intestinal flora diversity, structure, and phenotypic characteristics. H. pylori eradication efficacy was evaluated by 13C-urea breath test 4 weeks post-treatment. RESULTS The H. pylori eradication rates were 80.95% in group A and 75.00% in group B, with no statistical difference (χ 2 = 0.212, P = 0.719). Alpha diversity analysis showed that clarithromycin treatment (group B) significantly decreased ACE, Chao1, Sobs, and Shannon indices (all P < 0.05), while berberine treatment (group A) had no significant effect. Beta diversity and enterotype analysis revealed that clarithromycin induced significant changes in intestinal flora structure and enterotype distribution, whereas berberine maintained relatively stable flora structure. Neutral community model analysis indicated that berberine enhanced deterministic processes more significantly than clarithromycin in regulating flora assembly. Differential species analysis identified that Blautia was significantly enriched in group A post-treatment, and Dorea longicatena significantly enriched in group B. CONCLUSION Berberine exhibits comparable H. pylori eradication efficacy to clarithromycin, and has a milder impact on intestinal flora, maintaining flora homeostasis and reducing the risk of antibiotic resistance.

title: Spatiotemporal variability of extreme precipitation in Ecuador (1991-2020): wavelet coherence and non-parametric trend analysis by homogeneous zones
abstractText: The El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) phenomenon exerts a strong influence on precipitation variability in Ecuador, although its spatial impacts at the scale of homogeneous micro-basins and extreme events require more detailed analysis. This study assesses the relationship between ENSO and precipitation across 22 homogeneous zones of Ecuador for the 1991–2020 period. Using daily data from 433 meteorological stations quality-controlled and homogenized with Climatol, the daily regional precipitation signal was extracted using the first principal component (PC1) and physically scaled to millimeters (mm). The temporal relationship was evaluated using Wavelet Coherence (WTC) against the Niño 1 + 2 index, extracting high-frequency (2–4 years) and low-frequency (5–8 years) signals. Additionally, eight ETCCDI extreme precipitation indices were calculated on the daily physical PC1, and their trends were analyzed using linear regression and Mann-Kendall tests, alongside abrupt change detection with the Sequential Mann-Kendall method. The McNemar test revealed significant differences in the proportion of ENSO presence/absence between high and low frequencies in coastal and southern areas, specifically in Zones 2, 5, 7, 15, 18, 19, 20, and 22, reflecting scale-dependent climate responses. Extreme indices showed stability in most zones, with statistically significant upward trends localized in Zones 6, 8, and 21 (for RX1day) and Zones 19 and 20 (for PRCPTOT and R95p). Abrupt climate mutations concentrated during the 1992–1994, 1997–1998, and 2019–2020 periods. These findings demonstrate a marked spatial heterogeneity in extreme rainfall response to ENSO and reveal that high- and low-frequency signals modulate the climate differently across Ecuador, providing critical information for disaster risk management.

title: Fair division with binary valuations: Characterizations
abstractText: We consider the fair allocation of indivisible goods with binary valuations. In this setting, the maximum Nash welfare rule, the leximin rule, and all additive welfarist rules with a strictly concave function coincide. We show that for any number of agents, this rule is the only rule that satisfies envy-freeness up to one good, strategyproofness, neutrality, minimal completeness, and invariance under disapproving unassigned goods (IDU). Moreover, we present an alternative characterization for two agents, where we replace IDU with non-redundancy and resource-monotonicity. In both characterizations, all axioms are necessary.

title: The remotely sensed carousel of spring green-up: Do individual trees reshuffle their phenological ranks across years?
abstractText: Within temperate deciduous forests, spring leaf-out timing varies markedly among individuals of the same stand, yet whether this variation reflects persistent phenological strategies or year-specific reshuffling remains unresolved. Addressing this question requires individual-resolved, multi-year observations rarely achievable at scale with conventional monitoring. Here, we leveraged high-resolution PlanetScope satellite imagery, enabling individual crown resolution, to track spring canopy greenness of 50 European beech ( Fagus sylvatica ) individuals in a managed stand in the central Apennines (Tuscany, Italy) at five key stages of green-up over five years (2020–2024). We quantified intra-stand variability from green-up onset to the early summer canopy plateau and assessed the inter-annual consistency of within-stand phenological hierarchy using Kendall's coefficient of concordance and pairwise Spearman's rank correlations. Phenological ranks were significantly repeatable across years, yet consistency was strongly modulated by phenological phase. It peaked once canopy expansion was complete and collapsed during the preceding active leaf-expansion phase, which emerged as a tipping point where year-specific spring conditions most strongly reshuffled individual rank positions. At the individual level, four recurrent trajectory types were distinguished: trees with consistently high (consistently high archetype) or consistently low ranks (consistently low archetype), and two reshuffling types (variable archetypes) whose ranks changed in opposite directions between years. The coexistence of these strategies within a structurally homogeneous stand may reflect individual, possibly genetic, differences in phenological response and is consistent with a population-level bet-hedging mechanism, whereby phenological diversity buffers collective performance across variable spring conditions, distributing risk across the population rather than concentrating it. These findings challenge the assumption of fixed intra-population phenological niches and highlight the need for individual-scale frameworks in both empirical phenology and process-based modeling, particularly for southern populations facing accelerating climate change.

On the Convergence of the 11D M-Theory Action and Ramanujan Modular Symmetries: The Geometric Origin of the Nardelli Seventh-Root TOE Operator
abstractText: This paper presents the definitive formulation of the Nardelli Seventh-Root Theory of Everything (TOE) Master Equation, establishing a rigorous, UV-complete mathematical bridge between the continuous field actions of 11-dimensional M-Theory and the discrete landscape of analytical number theory. We demonstrate how the low-energy limit of 11D supergravity, modulated by M2/M5-brane gauge fluxes, undergoes a topological reduction when compactified over a 7-dimensional manifold of strict $G_2$ holonomy. By substituting standard local field-theoretic propagators with non-holomorphic harmonic Maass forms regularized via the Riemann Zeta function on the critical line $zeta(1/2+it)$ and an infinite-derivative wave kernel, we systematically eliminate perturbative quantum gravity divergences. The complete partition function—incorporating cosmological scalar fields $phi(t)$, supersymmetric mass thresholds $M_{text{SUSY}}$, and contour brane moduli integrals $int_{Gamma} |dmu|$—is anchored arithmetically by Ramanujan’s modular seeds (1729, 4096) and the modular discriminant $Delta$. We prove that under the action of the inverse 7th-root spatial operator, the transcendental degrees of freedom of the 11D supermultiplet identically contract onto the universal golden vacuum fixed point $phi approx 1.618665$, revealing a deterministic arithmetic design underlying the quantum vacuum.

title: Accurate spotlight spectra estimation using neural methods and compact disc diffraction gratings
abstractText: Inverse rendering and appearance modeling increasingly rely on accurate spectral modeling of scene illumination to synthesize photo-realistic images. However, measuring an illuminant’s spectral power distribution (SPD) using a spectroradiometer or hyperspectral imaging systems is costly and typically confined to specialized laboratories. We introduce an inexpensive, imaging-based method to estimate precise spotlight illumination SPDs by exploiting wavelength dependent diffraction patterns produced by a commercially available compact disc (CD). Our method captures rainbow-like diffraction rings produced by shining an unknown spotlight on a CD using a consumer grade camera, and (optionally) augments it with a color chart image for reliable spectral reconstruction of the spotlight illumination without needing explicit geometric or color calibration. Comprehensive qualitative and quantitative experiments on both physically based simulations and real-world images show that diffraction cues result in consistent high frequency spectral details that are hard to infer from a color chart alone. We assess the generalizability of our approach by evaluating it using 49 distinct (simulated) camera models including Nikon, Canon, Sony, iPhone and Samsung Galaxy. Furthermore, we examine the robustness of our method under manual flexibility in the placement and orientation of the compact disc where both can be easily constrained through quick visual inspections. Lastly, we validate the practical impact of our reconstructed SPDs through spectral inverse rendering of diffractive and iridescent materials, showing improved visual fidelity and reduced error.
