Esterified Banana Peel Waste as a Low-Cost Biosorbent for Heavy Metal Removal from Real Paint Manufacturing Wastewater: Effects of Concentration, pH, Contact Time, Dosage, and Regeneration
abstractText: The discharge of heavy metal-laden effluents from paint manufacturing operations is a significant and growing environmental hazard in industrialising economies, yet few biosorption studies test authentic multi-metal industrial effluent rather than synthetic single-metal solutions. This study investigates methanol/hydrochloric acid esterified banana peel waste (E-BPW) as a zero-cost biosorbent for removing chromium, nickel, cobalt, and lead from real paint manufacturing wastewater sourced from Brighto Paints Limited, Lahore, Pakistan. E-BPW was prepared by collection, drying, Tyler-standard sieve fractionation (850–1180 µm), and Fischer esterification with methanol and hydrochloric acid at 60°C for 48 h. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed carboxyl, hydroxyl, and ester carbonyl groups as the principal metal-binding moieties. Batch adsorption experiments evaluated the effects of initial metal concentration, solution pH, contact time, and adsorbent dosage, with metal concentrations quantified by flame atomic absorption spectroscopy. Under optimised conditions (pH 6–8, 80 min, 5 g·L⁻¹, 25°C), E-BPW achieved removal efficiencies of 80.3% (Cr), 68.9% (Co), 63.1% (Pb), and 56.0% (Ni). Regeneration with 2 mol·L⁻¹ HNO₃ recovered 99.3% of adsorbed metals, indicating strong potential for circular reuse. These findings demonstrate that waste-to-resource valorisation of agricultural byproducts can deliver technically effective, low-cost heavy metal removal for small-to-medium industrial applications, supporting Sustainable Development Goal 6 and circular-economy principles. The absence of isotherm, kinetic, and surface-characterisation data is acknowledged as a limitation, and a research agenda toward pilot-scale validation is proposed.

title: Allocation and greenhouse gas accounting for CO2 utilisation: a steelworks-to-fuel case study
abstractText: Carbon capture and utilisation (CCU) can convert industrial CO 2 -rich gases into fuels and chemicals, but reported climate benefits depend strongly on system boundaries, allocation and carbon accounting choices. This study assesses a multifunctional steelworks-to-fuel system in which blast furnace gas is conditioned and converted with hydrogen to produce a propane-rich fuel. Two perspectives are evaluated: a gate-to-gate CCU plant perspective (functional unit: 1 kg CO 2 -based fuel, a propane/butane/ethane mix) and a cradle-to-gate steel plant perspective (1 kg hot rolled coil, HRC). Global Warming Potential (GWP) is compared across hydrogen sources, embedded-carbon treatment, life-cycle assessment (LCA)-based allocation and the Renewable Energy Directive III (RED III) method for recycled carbon fuels. From the CCU perspective, production-stage GWP ranged from 1.97 to 7.69 kg CO 2 eq./kg without an embedded-carbon credit, exceeding the fossil reference mixture of 1.15; the credit reduced this to −1.03 to 4.69, where negative values reflect accounting rather than permanent storage. From the steel perspective, the benefit of diverting blast furnace gas is small (6%) and can become unfavourable when fuel credits are balanced as burdens on steel. Mass allocation assigns 1.86 kg CO 2 eq./kg to the fuel, above the fossil reference, whereas economic allocation assigns 1.03 kg CO 2 eq./kg (0.91‐1.19 across observed annual prices), below it at mean prices; under system expansion, HRC instead receives avoided-production credits and no separate fuel footprint is calculated. Under RED III, including the use phase, the fuel reaches 99 g CO 2 eq./MJ, above the 94 g CO 2 eq./MJ fossil fuel comparator, because the credit for the carbon input is balanced by combustion emissions while gas conditioning and lost electricity generation are charged to the fuel. CCU fuels therefore require transparent treatment of CO 2 inputs, displaced products and accounting boundaries to avoid misleading claims and misaligned incentives between CO 2 source and user.

title: From polyurethane waste to soil biostimulation: Microbial transformation and functional specialization of soil communities
abstractText: A new biostimulant product was obtained through a chemical process based on ozonolytic cleavage, which enables the depolymerisation of polyurethane in water. The resulting organic liquid extract (OLE), composed of low-molecular-weight carbon- and nitrogen-rich compounds, is susceptible to microbial metabolism by soil microorganisms. To evaluate its biostimulatory potential, the effects of different OLE concentrations on microbial activity, soil microbial community structure, and ecotoxicity towards Eisenia fetida were investigated. The results showed low toxicity to soil organisms, with adverse effects being observed only at high concentrations (104.8 g kg −1 ). Soil biostimulation assays revealed a dose-dependent stimulation of microbial activity, with dehydrogenase activity increasing more than fourfold compared with the control and fungal biomass reaching 1.96 ± 0.54 μg ergosterol g −1 in the OLE2 treatment. Functional prediction analysis using PICRUSt2 indicated shifts in the predicted functional profile of soil microbial communities following OLE application, particularly in pathways related to carbon metabolism, substrate transport, environmental sensing, and stress response. Overall, the results suggest that soil microorganisms may participate in the transformation of polyurethane-derived molecules, supporting the development of a sustainable two-phase chemical-biological strategy that integrates polyurethane waste valorization with soil biotechnology and circular bioeconomy approaches.

title: Liver abscess caused by Parvimonas micra originating from a fish bone: A case report
abstractText: BACKGROUND Liver abscess is an infectious lesion commonly caused by bacteria, Entamoeba histolytica , or fungi. Although Parvimonas micra (P. micra ) predominantly colonizes the orodigestive tract, liver abscesses associated with this bacterium are rarely reported. CASE SUMMARY A 52-year-old Chinese male patient presented to our emergency department with intermittent fever, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal distention for 12 days. These symptoms showed no significant improvement following treatment at the primary care hospital. Initial liver ultrasound revealed a 7 cm infectious left lobe lesion. Anaerobic blood cultures and matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry performed on admission and 2 days later both identified P. micra , suggesting that the liver abscess may have been caused by a foreign body originating from the digestive tract. Targeted examinations were performed. Abdomen enhanced computed tomography revealed a strip-shaped foreign body in the left outer lobe of the liver, extending to the wall of the pyloric canal. Simultaneous upper endoscopy and endoscopic ultrasonography detected a red scar in the gastric corpus and a 23.5 mm strip-shaped lesion within the liver mass, with one end penetrating the liver. The patient underwent laparoscopic left lateral liver lobectomy of the abscess and gastric perforation repair, during which a 3 cm fish bone was removed. He recovered fully after a targeted antibiotic regimen of penicillin G followed by piperacillin-tazobactam. This case is the first report of a liver abscess caused by P. micra due to ingestion of foreign bodies. CONCLUSION The clinical course of this patient highlights that the identification of P. micra and the detection of a foreign body within the liver mass provided pivotal clues for timely diagnosis and appropriate treatment.

Historical and projected changes in tropical North and South Atlantic indices under different emission scenarios
abstractText: Sea Surface Temperature (SST) variability in the Tropical North Atlantic (TNA) and Tropical South Atlantic (TSA) plays a critical role in regulating regional climate systems, atmospheric circulation, and hydrological extremes. However, uncertainties remain regarding the representation of tropical Atlantic SST variability and future warming patterns in CMIP6 climate models. This study investigated historical and projected SST anomaly characteristics over the TNA and TSA using NOAA ERSSTv5 observational data (1982--2014) and seven CMIP6 models under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios (1967--2099). Statistical analyses including Taylor diagrams, Mann--Kendall trend tests, Sen’s slope estimation, anomaly frequency analysis, and persistence assessment were employed to evaluate model performance and future variability. Results showed that CMIP6 models reasonably reproduced observed SST variability, with correlation coefficients ranging approximately from 0.65--0.88 for TSA and 0.55--0.85 for TNA. NOAA observations indicated stronger positive anomaly dominance over TSA (218 warm events) and comparatively higher negative anomaly frequency over TNA (206 cold events). Under SSP5-8.5, projected warming intensified substantially, with Sen’s slope values increasing up to 0.0057 and projected SST differences reaching 0.0387$^\circ$C in the TNA region. Persistence analysis further revealed prolonged consecutive SST anomaly events exceeding 150 months in some models under high-emission forcing. The findings suggest that enhanced greenhouse gas emissions may amplify tropical Atlantic variability, strengthen ocean--atmosphere feedbacks, and increase climate-related risks across West Africa and adjacent regions. This study provides important scientific evidence for improving climate projection reliability and supporting regional climate adaptation and risk management strategies.

title: Systemic immune and metabolomic responses to oral hyaluronic acid in a randomized placebo-controlled clinical study
abstractText: Oral hyaluronan (HA) supplementation has shown clinical benefits, but its systemic effects remain insufficiently characterized. We focused on the systemic effects of oral HA. (1.8 MDa) at 60 mg/day (SH60), 120 mg/day (SH120), or placebo for 12 weeks in 150 healthy donors. Within this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study, plasma samples were analyzed to assess changes in immune and metabolic markers, as well as alterations in lipid metabolism, using high-quality, untargeted omics approaches with high information depth. The SH120 group significantly reduced pro-inflammatory markers, including CRP, IL-1b, and precursor of inflammatory mediators such as arachidonic acid, compared with placebo. Together with selective modulation in metabolic biomarkers, including fetuin-A, adipsin, mannopyranosyl tryptophan, 1,16-hexadecanedioic acid, and 3-hydroxydecanoic acid, support the hypothesis that oral HA may promote an immune homeostasis and a “metabolically healthy” profile, exerting protective effects even in otherwise healthy individuals. Correlations between plasma markers and previously reported skin outcomes were generally weak, suggesting that modulation of systemic biomarkers can explain only partially the cutaneous effects of supplementation. Overall, oral HA was associated with selective changes in plasma biomarkers in healthy adults, which should be considered when evaluating the mechanisms underlying its clinical effects. title: Natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery: The true frontier of gastrointestinal endoscopy
abstractText: Natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (NOTES) remains a frontier that continues to blur the boundaries between surgery and interventional endoscopy. Since its inception as an idea, NOTES has witnessed remarkable progress, from early animal experiments to its gradual translation into human applications as a minimally invasive approach for various mediastinal, thoracic, peritoneal, retroperitoneal, and pelvic diseases. The initial phase of NOTES was met with significant technical and safety challenges, often requiring hybrid laparoscopic assistance. A decade after inception of the idea of NOTES, the first pure NOTES procedure, a transvaginal cholecystectomy, marked a turning point that demonstrated the feasibility of a completely incisionless surgical concept. Over time, major barriers such as safe access, reliable closure, and effective hemostasis have been steadily addressed through advances in endoscopic tunneling, suturing platforms, hemostatic materials, and flexible endoscopic systems. The evolution of third space endoscopy, endobariatric procedures, and organ preserving transluminal interventions has further strengthened the translational foundation of NOTES. Robotic are now providing greater stability, precision, and triangulation, bringing NOTES closer to daily clinical use. Now more than two decades since its conception, NOTES stands on the verge of redefining minimally invasive therapy. This review revisits its journey, summarizes the present achievements, and highlights the innovations and global collaboration needed to guide the next era of scarless surgery. Recent advances in magnetic-assisted platforms have also played an important role in improving exposure, traction, and anastomosis creation within NOTES.

title: Correlating Spin and Optical Properties of Quantum Emitters in hBN
abstractText: Optically addressable spin defects in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are well suited for near-surface quantum sensing. They offer bright, wavelength-tunable single-photon emission with high optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) contrast at room temperature. Here, we synthesize a high density of visible defects in carbon-doped hBN flakes with a high yield (14%) of ODMR-active emitters. We find that the zero-field splitting parameter D is directly correlated with the zero-phonon line of an emitter, while the ODMR contrast shows no such correlation. We further analyze an individual narrowband defect showing 68% ODMR contrast and enhance its photon collection by ∼40% using a solid immersion lens. By advancing both the practical synthesis of the spin complexes and the understanding of their microscopic origin, our results move us toward the deterministic creation of ODMR-active quantum emitters.

title: Low-background 3D Bi2WO6 enables in situ sulfidation-induced photocurrent polarity switching for highly selective photoelectrochemical detection of sulfide ions
abstractText: Regulating photocurrent polarity is of significant importance for constructing photoelectrochemical (PEC) sensing platforms with enhanced sensitivity and reliability in practical applications. However, the intrinsically high background photocurrent in conventional PEC systems often masks analyte-induced signal variations, thereby hindering reliable photocurrent polarity switching. Herein, we report a low-background polarity-switchable PEC sensing platform based on three-dimensional (3D) flower-like Bi 2 WO 6 for the highly selective detection of S 2- . Benefiting from its intrinsically low background cathodic photocurrent and hierarchical nanosheet-assembled architecture, the constructed 3D Bi 2 WO 6 PEC platform exhibits a wide linear range (0-13.3 µM), a low detection limit of 16 nM outperforming the 2D Bi 2 WO 6 counterpart and most previously reported PEC sensing systems for S 2- detection, as well as excellent anti-interference capability and reliable analytical performance in complex real samples. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the hierarchical 3D architecture facilitates local S 2- enrichment and accelerates the in situ surface sulfidation process, leading to the rapid formation of a direct Z-scheme Bi 2 WO 6 /Bi 2 S 3 heterojunction. This target-triggered interfacial reconstruction dynamically reverses the dominant charge-carrier migration pathway, thereby inducing a distinct photocurrent transition from cathodic to anodic. This work provides an effective strategy for ultrasensitive S 2- detection and offers new insights into the design of low-background PEC sensors with dynamically tunable signal outputs.

title: Beyond interpersonal disputes: a text network analysis of conflict and negative communication experiences among experienced nurses
abstractText: Background Experienced nurses are defined in this study as nurses with at least two years of clinical experience. They deliver direct patient care, educate junior staff, and coordinate teams. Conflict and negative communication involving this group have been linked to burnout, turnover, and compromised patient safety, yet the semantic structure of these experiences remains poorly understood. Conflict serves here as a conceptual frame, not a separately measured outcome. This study aims to identify core keywords and the semantic structure of these experiences using text network analysis (TNA). Methods The dataset comprised 1,116 free-text narrative entries from 392 experienced nurses across 14 sessions of a Positive Organizational Culture Workshop (August 2021–February 2023) at a tertiary general hospital in South Korea. After preprocessing with three user-defined dictionaries, a co-occurrence network of adjacent terms within sentences (window size two) was constructed in NetMiner 4.5.1.e. The 30 most frequent keywords formed a network of 161 links; after links occurring only once were removed, 86 links remained. Degree, closeness, and betweenness centrality and modularity-based communities were computed on this binary, undirected network, and sensitivity to these two settings was examined. Results Four keywords ranked within the top five on all three centrality measures: “physician in charge,” “phone call,” “family member,” and “senior nurse.” Community detection (modularity = 0.24) suggested five exploratory semantic communities: repeated explanation and complaints from family members; anger and shouting directed at the primary nurse over the phone; orders, verification, and requests involving the physician in charge and other departments; verbal abuse and irritation when reporting to the on-call physician; and hierarchy, handover, and reprimand among nurses. Labels were assigned after reviewing the original narratives. The two highest-ranked keywords in degree centrality were unchanged across alternative settings, whereas community membership varied. Conclusions The reported experiences were structured around telephone-mediated communication with the physician in charge, explanation demands and complaints from patients’ family members, and hierarchical relationships among nurses. The perceived repetition of such experiences was embedded in the family-related community. These concepts may warrant organizational attention in conflict management, and their value as intervention targets remains to be tested. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Single-cell transcriptomic profiling reveals novel stem cell markers for corneal limbal epithelium homeostasis
abstractText: Sox9 is a well-established marker of skin epithelial hair follicle stem cells and has been observed in the corneal limbus of Sox9-EGFP transgenic mice. Using Sox9-EGFP as a reference marker, this study characterized the transcriptomic atlas of corneal limbal epithelial cells during homeostasis and identified novel markers of limbal stem cells (LSCs) by single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq). A total of 20,351 viable cells were profiled, revealing 13 distinct cell clusters with unique molecular signatures. The cluster enriched with EGFP-positive cells was identified as the putative LSCs population during corneal epithelial homeostasis. Comparative analysis of corneal LSCs and early differentiated cells revealed several differentially expressed genes (DEGs) strongly associated with stemness-related pathways, including Gabrp , Fmo1 , Fmo2 , and Alcam , which were identified as potential novel LSC markers. Among these DEGs, Gabrp , and Alcam were exclusively expressed in the limbus, as confirmed by quantitative PCR (qPCR), Western blotting, and immunofluorescence staining. This study delineated the heterogeneous cellular composition of the limbal epithelium and uncovered several novel candidate markers that may be critical for maintaining corneal epithelial homeostasis.

title: CCTA-derived anatomical features and exploratory risk stratification of severe stent-jailed left circumflex coronary artery narrowing for non-true left main bifurcation lesions
abstractText: Purpose Provisional stenting is recommended in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for non-true left main bifurcation lesions (LMBLs); however, unexpected severe stent-jailed left circumflex coronary artery (LCX) narrowing is a clinical concern, and its prediction remains challenging. This study aimed to investigate anatomical features associated with LCX narrowing following provisional stenting for non-true LMBLs without significant LCX lesions and to derive an exploratory risk score using coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA). Methods This was a multicenter retrospective observational study that enrolled patients who underwent CCTA before PCI for non-true LMBLs with provisional stenting from December 2019 to May 2024. Quantitative CCTA analysis of LMBL was performed, and severe stent-jailed LCX narrowing, defined as angiographic stenosis ≥ 90%, was assessed. Anatomical features associated with LCX narrowing were identified using multivariable analysis, and a CCTA-derived exploratory risk score was derived. Results Overall, 109 patients were recruited, 16 (14.7%) of whom had severe stent-jailed LCX narrowing. Multivariable analysis identified the following parameters as associated with LCX narrowing: left anterior descending artery–LCX vessel angle ≤ 86°, area stenosis (AS) of the distal LM (LMd) ≥ 54%, AS of the ostial LCX ≥ 63%, and calcium thickness of the LMd ≥ 0.5 mm. An exploratory risk score based on these four features showed a stepwise increase in the incidence of severe LCX narrowing, with a C-statistic of 0.877. Conclusion CCTA identified anatomical features associated with severe stent-jailed LCX narrowing following provisional stenting. An exploratory risk score was derived from these features.

title: Multimorbidity patterns, disease networks, and phenotype clusters in Vietnamese children
abstractText: Multimorbidity in children remains poorly characterized in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), with no prior large-scale network-analytic study in Vietnam. We aimed to describe the prevalence, structure, and demographic determinants of pediatric multimorbidity using a population-level school health database. We analyzed 283,926 annual school health visits from 72,909 children aged 0 to 18 years attending a private school system in Vietnam (2020 to 2025). Multimorbidity was defined as ≥ 2 ICD-10 diagnoses per child. A six-layer multiplex network was constructed to identify disease hubs via betweenness centrality. Temporal trajectories were assessed with directed binomial tests, and multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios for comorbidity pairs. Association rules were extracted via Apriori and phenotype clusters were derived using Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) followed by Leiden community detection. Multimorbidity was present in 53.7% of children, with higher burden in males (55.7% vs. 51.5%) and the 6 to 11-year age group (65.7%). The strongest co-occurrences involved blindness/low vision with protein-energy malnutrition (OR 6.71) and hyperalimentation (OR 8.73), constituting a visual-nutritional double burden. Acute tonsillitis and dental caries emerged as the top universal disease hubs (hub scores 1.10 and 0.95, respectively). Hyperalimentation preceding obesity was the highest-risk temporal sequence (RR 2.45). Seven phenotype clusters were identified (multimorbidity prevalence 39.3% to 69.5%), with disorders of refraction and dental caries present across all groups. Multimorbidity is highly prevalent in this urban Vietnamese pediatric population. A nutritional-ophthalmological cluster and an upper airway-oral health cluster support integrated school-based screening and interventions in Vietnam and comparable LMICs.

title: Bimetallic synergy and electronic Metal-Support Interaction in PtCu/CeO2 catalysts to Steer furfural Hydro-Rearrangement
ZIF-8-derived Cu–Zn–Zr mixed oxide catalysts for selective electrochemical CO2 reduction to methanol
abstractText: The selective electrochemical reduction of CO 2 to methanol offers a promising route for carbon utilization, although achieving high efficiency and selectivity remains challenging. In this study, we prepared a series of Cu–Zn–Zr mixed-oxide catalysts by carbonizing a ZIF-8-based precursor containing copper and zirconium at 600 °C under nitrogen. Structural characterization by XRD, SEM, and EDX mapping showed the formation of monoclinic CuO, hexagonal ZnO, and tetragonal ZrO 2 phases, with nanoscale particle agglomerates and a uniform spatial distribution of Cu, Zn, and Zr throughout the catalyst. Among the compositions studied, the catalyst with 15% copper content (CuZnZr-15) showed the most favorable structural features and gave the best performance, reaching a Faradaic efficiency of 48.9% for methanol at a partial current density of 39.6 mA cm −2 . The improved activity is attributed to the coexistence of overlapping distributions of CuO, ZnO, and t-ZrO 2 phases, which is proposed to facilitate CO 2 activation and stabilize key intermediates. These findings show that ZIF-8-derived Cu–Zn–Zr oxide catalysts provide an effective platform for selective electrochemical CO 2 -to-methanol conversion.

title: Light Transmission through Multilayer Metal Gratings with Periodic Slit Array Structures
abstractText: We design a multilayer periodic metallic silver film grating with a slit array structure and investigate its electromagnetic transmission characteristics using the rigorous coupled-wave analysis (RCWA) method. The physical mechanism underlying the extraordinary optical transmission (EOT) phenomenon is elucidated through steady-state field distribution analysis. Our results reveal significant modifications in the transmission spectrum when transitioning from a single-layer to a multilayer grating configuration. Calculations of the steady-state electromagnetic field distribution demonstrate enhanced field coupling at transmission wavelengths associated with EOT. The magnetic field enhancement is attributed to surface plasmon resonance occurring both between adjacent silver film layers and within the slits. We conclude that the EOT behavior in metal grating slit arrays originates from the coupling resonance of surface plasmons at the metal–dielectric interface; under this resonance condition, the metallic silver film grating structure exhibits pronounced EOT.

title: Coronary artery calcium burden and coronary CT angiography evaluability in patients undergoing hemodialysis
abstractText: Purpose To investigate the association between coronary artery calcium (CAC) burden and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) evaluability in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis. Methods This retrospective single-center study included 65 patients who underwent CAC scoring and CCTA. The right coronary artery, left anterior descending artery, and left circumflex artery were independently assessed by two blinded observers using a four-point image-quality scale. Arteries scored 3 or 4 were considered evaluable, and limited evaluability was defined as at least one non-evaluable major coronary artery. Associations were assessed using Spearman correlation, established CAC-score categories, receiver operating characteristic analysis with bootstrap confidence intervals, and multivariable logistic regression. Results The median total CAC score was 671 (interquartile range, 251–1,774). All three major coronary arteries were evaluable in 26 patients (40.0%), whereas 39 (60.0%) had limited evaluability. Median CAC scores increased stepwise as the number of evaluable arteries decreased from three to zero (162.5, 677.0, 1,663.0, and 2,180.0; Spearman’s ρ = −0.608, P < 0.001). CAC score ≥ 400 was associated with limited evaluability (odds ratio, 6.30; 95% CI, 2.10–18.90; P < 0.001). The AUC was 0.831 (bootstrap 95% CI, 0.723–0.925). After adjustment for age and sex, each approximate doubling of CAC score was associated with higher odds of limited evaluability (adjusted odds ratio, 2.01; 95% CI, 1.40–2.88; P < 0.001). Conclusion Increasing CAC burden was associated with a progressive reduction in CCTA evaluability in patients undergoing hemodialysis. CAC scoring may help anticipate technical limitations of CCTA and inform coronary imaging strategy.

title: Positive selection tends to act on exposed extracellular regions and delineate interaction modules targeted by pathogens
abstractText: Background Positive selection shapes protein function by favoring amino acid substitutions that increase fitness. Although numerous studies have identified positively selected genes (PSGs), the structural principles underlying residue-level positive selection remain incompletely understood and previous studies have produced conflicting conclusions, particularly regarding the preferential location of positively selected residues (PSRs) within intrinsically disordered regions. In order to resolve these issues and to better understand the driving forces underlying positive selection in human proteins, we performed a comprehensive analysis on a manually curated, high-quality collection of PSGs and PSRs as well as on a large-scale PSR dataset restricted to proteins with experimental structures. Results Human PSRs were significantly enriched in secreted and cell membrane proteins and preferentially localized to extracellular regions, solvent-exposed protein surfaces, coil structures, and protein-protein interaction interfaces, whereas neither domains nor intrinsically disordered regions showed an enrichment. Spatial clustering analysis reinforced that PSRs accumulate within localized surface patches. Integration of host-pathogen interaction data highlighted that adaptive changes preferentially affect extracellular molecular recognition surfaces, recurrently appearing in certain pathogen-interacting membrane protein families and particular domain types. Additionally, PSRs showed an enrichment in the residues of human-pathogen interaction interfaces that are in direct contact with pathogenic proteins, implying that neutralizing pathogen attacks is one of the driving forces behind the adaptive evolution of human proteins. By analysing human variation data we found that PSRs are enriched in benign but depleted in pathogenic substitutions, extending previous observations that positively selected genes contain elevated levels of missense variation. Notably, PSGs of the large-scale dataset were also enriched among clinical-stage drug targets, suggesting a potential link between positive selection and pharmacological relevance. Conclusion Together, our results provide a refined structural model of adaptive evolution in human proteins and identify extracellular exposed molecular recognition surfaces and human-pathogen interaction interfaces as recurrent hotspots of positive selection. Our results point to the direction that precise identification of human PSRs could delineate important host-pathogen interfaces that exert evolutionary selection pressure on humans and appoint novel targets with therapeutic potential.

title: Barriers to the integration of mental health services into HIV and TB care: a mixed-methods assessment in high-volume healthcare facilities in Niger State, Nigeria
abstractText: Background HIV and tuberculosis (TB) remain major public health challenges in Sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in Nigeria, where mental health disorders such as depression and anxiety further compromise adherence to antiretroviral therapy (ART) and directly observed therapy (DOT). Despite this, mental health services remain poorly integrated into healthcare delivery. This baseline assessment evaluated the availability and integration of mental health services in selected facilities in Niger state, in line with Nigeria's national mental health policies. Method A mixed-method cross-sectional design was employed, using cluster sampling to select six facilities across the state and purposive sampling to identify those with the highest ART client load. Quantitative data were collected using assessment checklists and service utilization records, while qualitative data were obtained through key informant interviews (KIIs) with heads of ART, DOT, and Mental Health units. Quantitative analysis using STATA generated percentages, and qualitative data were thematically analyzed. Results Findings showed no integration of mental health services within ART and DOT units across all facilities (0%). Only 25% of facilities had a dedicated mental health desk, adequate workforce, data capturing tools, or safe counselling space. Mental health policies and SOPs (6.3%) and dedicated budgets (6.3%) were largely absent. Referral directories (25%), inter-facility partnerships (12.5%), and support groups (12.5%) were also limited. Overall, the results indicate weak structural readiness and lack of integration of mental health services within HIV and TB care settings. Conclusion The study highlights a critical gap in mental health service integration within HIV and TB care. Considering the rate of professionals compared to demands, training and task-shifting approaches will help expand service delivery, integration of routine screening tools into ART and DOT clinics and strengthening of referral systems through structured directories and digital linkage mechanisms. In addition, tele-mental health support systems are recommended to improve access and continuity of care.

title: Ketahanan Budaya Masyarakat Lokal di Tengah Tekanan Pariwisata Global: Studi Mixed Methods di Destinasi Strategis Bali
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis ketahanan budaya masyarakat lokal dalam menghadapi tekanan pariwisata global di Bali. Menggunakan pendekatan mixed methods, penelitian ini mengombinasikan data kuantitatif dari survei terhadap masyarakat lokal dan data kualitatif dari wawancara mendalam serta observasi partisipatif di kawasan Ubud, Kuta, Seminyak, dan Nusa Dua. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa tekanan pariwisata global, terutama dalam bentuk overtourism, homogenisasi budaya, dan komodifikasi, berpengaruh signifikan terhadap perubahan sosial-budaya masyarakat lokal. Namun demikian, masyarakat menunjukkan kapasitas adaptif melalui berbagai mekanisme ketahanan budaya, seperti revitalisasi tradisi dan pengembangan community-based tourism. Penelitian ini menegaskan bahwa ketahanan budaya berperan sebagai variabel mediasi yang menentukan keberlanjutan budaya lokal.

title: Papers Without Code: Availability of GitHub Repositories Linked in *CL Publications
abstractText: Source code and data published at computational linguistics (*CL) venues are increasingly being shared via GitHub. While this generally is a favorable development for the accessibility and potential reusability of research artifacts in natural language processing (NLP), the long-term availability of such repositories has not been evaluated. In this squib, we discuss the availability of repositories linked in papers published in the Computational Linguistics (CL) journal as well as at ACL and its co-located events over the past ten years. Contrary to our expectations, we find that GitHub repositories linked in more recent ACL publications are unavailable at similar rates as in older publications, in part due to an increase in empty and placeholder repositories. Similar trends hold for other *CL venues, but not for platforms other than GitHub.

title: Construction of Methodology for Mapping Fish Farming in the Legal Amazon
abstractText: Pisciculture has been established as a strategic activity in the Amazon, with emphasis on the cultivation of tambaqui (Colossoma macropomum) and its hybrids. This study analyzed the spatial dynamics of aquaculture in three municipalities of the Legal Amazon: Ariquemes (RO), Sorriso (MT) and Paragominas (PA), using geotechnologies and remote sensing. Using Sentinel-2 images, Google Earth Engine and the DBSCAN algorithm, excavated tanks were mapped, analyzed in terms of area, perimeter, compactness and spatial organization. The average area of the nurseries was 0.57 ha, higher than the national average. There was high structural and productive variability among the municipalities. Ariquemes had larger and more compact nurseries, while Paragominas stood out for the irregularity in the shapes of the tanks. The multivariate analysis indicated that factors such as urban proximity, logistical infrastructure and level of technification directly influence the distribution and performance of fish farming. It was also observed the coexistence between small producers and large enterprises, revealing a heterogeneous production structure. Among the challenges identified, we highlight the low spatial resolution of images, the overlap of structures and inappropriate environmental practices, such as stream barrages, which make it difficult to distinguish between natural water bodies and excavated tanks. It is concluded that the integration between geotechnologies and socioeconomic data is essential for the sustainable planning of aquaculture in the region. Regional public policies, infrastructure improvement and incentives for environmental regularization are fundamental to the strengthening and sustainability of the sector.

title: Filtering LLM-Synthesized Data for Cold-Start Recommendation: A Progressive Influence Function Approach
abstractText: Leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs)-synthesized data to enable representation learning for cold-start entities has emerged as a promising solution for addressing cold-start recommendations. However, existing studies often over-rely on LLM-generated data while neglecting the detrimental noise it may introduce. This work investigates data filtering mechanisms to remove detrimental synthetic samples. One promising approach is to use influence functions to measure the influence of each data. Nevertheless, a technical challenge arises because accurate influence estimation requires an unbiased reference model, which cannot be satisfied due to the existence of unknown noise. To address this, we conduct a theoretical analysis, revealing that when the goal is to identify a small subset of highly harmful data, even a biased model can still reliably capture the most detrimental points. Building on this insight, we propose a Progressive Influence Function (PIF)-based method for data filtering. PIF iteratively refines influence estimates: it repeatedly trains a new reference model after removing the previous step’s most harmful data and reassesses influence. As detrimental data is progressively removed, the reference model becomes less biased. Finally, PIF ensembles influence estimates across iterations for robust filtering. Extensive experiments validate the efficacy of our approach.

title: Intent Representation and Human Distraction Modulate the Effects of Legible Robot Motion in Hallway Navigation
abstractText: Legibility in human-robot interaction (HRI) is often described as the property of robot motion that enables an observer to confidently and quickly infer the robot’s intent. Mature frameworks exist for generating legible motion in front of static observers, typically by making the robot’s destination apparent as early as possible. Social robot navigation in public spaces, however, presents a different challenge: pedestrians are themselves in motion, often with divided attention, and must coordinate with the robot in real time. In such encounters, where the robot is ultimately headed may matter less to a pedestrian than how it intends to pass them. This raises two questions: which aspect of intent should legible motion convey, and does legibility remain beneficial when pedestrians are not fully attentive to the robot? We address these questions in the ubiquitous and demanding scenario of hallway navigation, through two controlled user studies comparing multiple legibility formulations implemented within a shared model predictive control framework. Study 1 ( N = 45) compares destination-based and passing-side intent representations, showing that the latter, particularly when adaptively updated, allows for smoother human motion and is perceived as more competent and less mentally and physically demanding than the former. Study 2 ( N = 45) examines the effect of pedestrian attention, demonstrating that legible motion supports smooth human motion even under distraction, although this benefit is not consistently reflected in subjective ratings. Together, these findings suggest that effective legible motion in social robot navigation benefits from interaction-level intent representations that support coordination, with some effects persisting even when human attention is divided. Code is available at https://github.com/fluentrobotics/Legible_MPPI and footage from our experiments at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P5O5BwfcUCo .

title: Synergistic Dual-Modification of Polyurethane Sponge with MIL-53(Al) and Dimethylsilicone Oil for Efficient Oil–Water Separation of Oily Sludge Thermal Washing Wastewater
abstractText: Developing highly efficient adsorbents is one of the most feasible strategies to achieve oil-water separation. Conventional sponge adsorbents often suffer from limited capacity, poor cyclic stability, and low selectivity. To overcome these limitations, in this study, we synergistically modified a commercial polyurethane sponge using MIL-53(Al) and dimethylsilicone oil (DMS) via a facile dip-coating strategy, resulting in the M/Si-6@PU sponge. Through the optimization of the synthesis process, the dual-modified sponge evinced a water contact angle of 140° and an oil contact angle of 0° in air. This super-wetting property significantly accelerated the oil absorption process, reducing the absorption time by 48% (2.6 s compared to 5.0 s for the pristine polyurethane (PU) sponge). Meanwhile, this sponge exhibited outstanding adsorption capacities for various oils, including toluene (43 g·g − 1 ), pump oil (40 g·g − 1 ), diesel (39 g·g − 1 ), vegetable oil (35 g·g − 1 ), soybean oil (33 g·g − 1 ), and real oily wastewater (31 g·g − 1 ). Furthermore, the sponge maintained a high separation efficiency (> 99.0%) for oily sludge thermal washing wastewater over 8 cycles, with the efficiency remaining robust at 93.6% after 30 cycles. The composite also exhibited excellent chemical stability, retaining its hydrophobicity after 1 h of immersion in extreme pH environments (pH = 1 and 12). Therefore, the synergistic combination of hierarchical roughness and low surface energy renders the M/Si-6@PU sponge a highly promising candidate for practical and harsh industrial oily wastewater treatments.

title: Geochemical characteristics and genesis of urban surface-deposited sediments: a parallel investigation across a network of small Russian cities
abstractText: Purpose This study tests the hypothesis that the physicochemical characteristics and reproducible geochemical-mineralogical relationships of urban surface-deposited sediments are fundamentally controlled by the combined effects of the local lithogenic substrate, anthropogenic material inputs, and landscape conditions governing sediment production. To address this, a comparative study was conducted using a consistent sampling and analytical framework across cities with contrasting geological and anthropogenic characteristics. Methods A total of 300 sediment samples were collected from eight cities within the Sverdlovsk Oblast, Russia. A detailed landscape survey was conducted to document the general characteristics of each sampling site and the local catchment area from which the sediment was mobilized. Chemical, mineralogical, and particle-size analyses of the sediments were performed. Results The results indicate that while the sediments mineral composition is rooted in the local geological parent material, it has been significantly modified by minerals sourced from regional mining operations and utilized in construction. A unique mineralogical assemblage formed in each city governs the specific elemental baseline profile. The fine fraction (< 100 µm) proportion depends on the mineral characteristics, which can be attributed to the varying resistance of minerals to weathering in the urban environment. The main landscape factors influencing the fine fraction generation are terrain slope and disturbed surfaces. Conclusion Acting cumulatively, natural and anthropogenic drivers turn surface-deposited sediments into a comprehensive geochemical archive. A systemic understanding of the core physicochemical properties of the sediments serves as a fundamental prerequisite for effectively investigating the environmental implications of urban sedimentogenesis.

title: Aislamiento social y su efecto en la salud mental de adultos mayores: revisión narrativa
abstractText: Se analizó el efecto del aislamiento social en la salud mental de los adultos mayores y las estrategias para prevenirlo. Se realizó una revisión narrativa de la literatura indexada en PubMed, SciELO y Redalyc y se incluyeron siete estudios publicados entre 2021 y 2024. La soledad se asoció con depresión, ansiedad, deterioro cognitivo y mayor mortalidad; su prevalencia en Europa varió entre el 10 % y el 33,4 %. El aislamiento social elevó el riesgo de demencia (HR 1,26) y se relacionó con menor volumen de sustancia gris, peor memoria y atención y mayor cortisol. El uso de internet se acompañó de menos síntomas depresivos y de redes de apoyo más amplias. La valoración enfermera del aislamiento y de la soledad, junto con intervenciones comunitarias, psicológicas y tecnológicas, protege la salud mental de esta población.

title: Prevalencia de la obesidad infantil y su relación con enfermedades crónicas: revisión narrativa
abstractText: Se analizó la prevalencia de la obesidad infantil y su relación con enfermedades crónicas mediante una revisión narrativa en PubMed y SciELO; se incluyeron 8 estudios publicados entre 2019 y 2024. La obesidad afectó al 7,0 % de las niñas y al 7,1 % de los niños de 3 a 4 años de Barcelona, al 17,3 % de los escolares españoles de 6 a 9 años y al 18,1 % de los escolares mexicanos, y fue mayor en barrios de menor nivel socioeconómico. El consumo sostenido de ultraprocesados, el sedentarismo y el entorno social se asociaron con el exceso de peso. La hipertensión fue más frecuente con exceso de peso (hasta 15,27 % frente a 1,90 %) y el síndrome metabólico afectó al 2,8 % de niños y 4,8 % de adolescentes. Se requieren detección temprana, educación familiar y acciones escolares con participación de enfermería.

title: Importancia del lavado de manos para prevenir enfermedades infecciosas en comerciantes del Mercado Central
abstractText: Se analizó el lavado de manos como medida de prevención de enfermedades infecciosas en los comerciantes del Mercado Central de Tulcán, desde la teoría del entorno de Florence Nightingale. Se realizó un estudio cuantitativo, descriptivo y transversal; de una población de 170 trabajadores se encuestó a una muestra aleatoria de 90 (confianza del 90 %, error del 6 %) con un cuestionario cerrado. El 92,2 % tenía acceso a agua y jabón y el 83,3 % usaba jabón al lavarse las manos. Después de tocar dinero o superficies compartidas, el 33,7 % se lavaba siempre las manos y el 42,7 % a veces. El 81,1 % creía que el lavado previene enfermedades y el 28,9 % lo promovía siempre entre compañeros y clientes. Los comerciantes reconocen la utilidad del lavado de manos, pero lo practican de forma irregular; se requieren educación sanitaria y un suministro constante de agua y jabón.

title: Estrategias de manejo del estrés en enfermeras de unidades de cuidados intensivos: revisión bibliográfica
abstractText: Se identificaron las estrategias de manejo del estrés descritas para enfermeras de unidades de cuidados intensivos. Se realizó una revisión bibliográfica narrativa de nueve estudios publicados entre 2014 y 2021 y localizados en PubMed, SciELO y Dialnet, agrupados en factores de estrés e intervenciones. El agotamiento se asoció con las horas nocturnas, el número de pacientes por turno, la falta de personal y el ruido, y el apoyo social moderó su relación con la ansiedad. El entrenamiento cognitivo-conductual y el mindfulness redujeron el estrés laboral y el cansancio emocional; los programas de mindfulness y resiliencia fueron factibles y el yoga redujo el cansancio emocional. Las recomendaciones de expertos priorizaron cambios en el entorno de trabajo. El manejo del estrés en enfermeras de cuidados intensivos combina intervenciones individuales con medidas institucionales sobre la dotación de personal, los turnos y el apoyo social.

title: Efectividad de intervenciones basadas en los 10 correctos de enfermería: revisión narrativa
abstractText: Se analizó la evidencia sobre intervenciones de enfermería alineadas con los 10 correctos para prevenir errores en la administración de medicamentos intravenosos. Se realizó una revisión narrativa de 13 estudios publicados entre 2008 y 2021, tomados de las referencias de una revisión sistemática previa y verificados en PubMed, SciELO o el sitio del editor. Los errores de preparación variaron entre estudios y fueron menores en la farmacia central que en las salas. En 2008 infusiones hubo errores en el 11,5 % y discrepancias en el 53,0 %; las bombas inteligentes no modificaron la tasa de error. Un protocolo dirigido por enfermeras logró el antibiótico en la primera hora en el 96,4 % de 697 pacientes. La formación, las listas de verificación y los sistemas de circuito cerrado se asociaron con prácticas más seguras. Los protocolos estandarizados y la capacitación continua sostienen la aplicación de los 10 correctos.

title: Impresión 3D y tecnología CAD/CAM en la fabricación de prótesis dentales personalizadas
abstractText: Esta revisión analizó la evidencia sobre la impresión 3D y la tecnología CAD/CAM en la fabricación de prótesis dentales personalizadas, con énfasis en precisión, materiales, eficiencia y desenlaces clínicos. Se realizó una revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed, Scopus y la Biblioteca Cochrane (2016-2024), que incluyó 15 documentos. Las prótesis totales fresadas mostraron mayor exactitud y mejores propiedades mecánicas que las impresas y las convencionales; los flujos digitales redujeron citas, tiempo clínico y costes, con satisfacción comparable. Los materiales impresos para restauraciones definitivas carecen de seguimiento clínico prolongado, y el coste de los equipos, la formación y los residuos limitaron su adopción. Ambas tecnologías optimizan la rehabilitación protésica y requieren protocolos estandarizados y formación.

title: Higiene bucal e innovación tecnológica: hábitos, placa bacteriana y caries en adultos de Quevedo
abstractText: Este estudio describió los hábitos de higiene bucal y su relación con la placa, la caries y la enfermedad periodontal en adultos de Quevedo, Ecuador. Se realizó un estudio cuantitativo, descriptivo y transversal en 40 personas de 18 a 50 años, con cuestionario estructurado y examen clínico (índice de Silness y Löe). El 85 % se cepillaba al menos dos veces al día, pero solo el 40 % usaba hilo dental regularmente; el 65 % presentó placa moderada o abundante y el 50 %, caries, más frecuente sin hilo dental (58,3 % frente a 37,5 %; p = 0,197). El cepillado aislado resultó insuficiente; la limpieza interdental y la tecnología deben complementar la educación preventiva.

title: Factores epidemiológicos que influyen en pacientes mayores de 60 años con diabetes mellitus tipo 2
abstractText: Se analizaron los factores epidemiológicos asociados con la prevalencia, el control y las complicaciones de la diabetes mellitus tipo 2 en personas mayores de 60 años. Se realizó una revisión narrativa de cuatro estudios observacionales y cuatro metaanálisis publicados entre 2000 y 2024 e indizados en PubMed y SciELO. En una población rural de Ecuador, la probabilidad de diabetes aumentó un 6 % por cada año de edad y la prevalencia fue mayor en mujeres. La neuropatía fue la complicación más frecuente y la polifarmacia afectó al 30,2 % de quienes tenían diabetes e hipertensión. La baja posición socioeconómica elevó el riesgo de diabetes, la depresión se asoció con hiperglucemia y solo el 54 % de los pacientes cumplió el tratamiento oral. La edad, la obesidad, el sedentarismo, la desigualdad social y la salud mental condicionan la enfermedad y orientan el tamizaje y la educación de enfermería.

title: Factores de riesgo contribuyentes a la diabetes mellitus en adolescentes: revisión narrativa
abstractText: Se analizaron los factores de riesgo de diabetes mellitus en adolescentes, en especial de la tipo 2. Se realizó una revisión narrativa de seis estudios publicados entre 2010 y 2024 y localizados en SciELO, PubMed, Medigraphic y sitios de revistas. La obesidad, el sedentarismo, la mala alimentación y los antecedentes familiares se asociaron con resistencia a la insulina y debut temprano. En adolescentes cubanos predominaron el consumo insuficiente de frutas y verduras (81,25 %) y el sedentarismo (45,83 %); el 72,92 % reunía tres o más factores. En adolescentes peruanos, la prevalencia de síndrome metabólico varió entre 4,3 % y 17,1 % según el criterio diagnóstico. En la diabetes tipo 1, la implicación familiar y el apoyo emocional condicionaron la calidad de vida. La prevención exige detectar pronto los factores modificables y educar en salud desde la familia, la escuela y los servicios sanitarios.

title: Cuidados básicos de enfermería en pacientes paliativos: revisión de la literatura
abstractText: Se describieron los cuidados básicos de enfermería en pacientes paliativos y su efecto en el control de síntomas, el confort y la calidad de vida. Se realizó una revisión narrativa de diez documentos (2009-2021) localizados en PubMed, SciELO y ScienceDirect, con síntesis en cinco dominios de cuidado. La atención paliativa temprana mejoró la calidad de vida y redujo los síntomas depresivos; la educación sobre analgesia disminuyó la intensidad del dolor. La higiene oral mejoró la xerostomía y el 86,6 % de los pacientes refirió confort alto. Las úlceras por presión afectaron al 18,8 % de los pacientes en atención domiciliaria. La atención domiciliaria aumentó la probabilidad de morir en casa y la atención temprana redujo la depresión de los cuidadores. El control de síntomas, el cuidado de la piel y la boca, la nutrición individualizada y el apoyo emocional y familiar forman el núcleo del cuidado enfermero paliativo.

title: Efectos de la falta de sueño en bienestar y rendimiento de profesionales de la salud
abstractText: Se analizaron los factores asociados a la privación de sueño en profesionales de la salud y sus efectos en el bienestar y el rendimiento. Se realizó una revisión narrativa de seis estudios publicados entre 2021 y 2024 y localizados en SciELO, Elsevier y Google Académico. El 35 % de los médicos residentes no cumplía los descansos obligatorios tras la guardia; en especialidades quirúrgicas, el 70 %. En un hospital ecuatoriano, el 34 % tuvo problemas con pacientes por cansancio. En estudiantes de salud, la mala calidad del sueño pasó del 24,90 % al 54,36 % en un semestre; en otro grupo predominaron letargo y ansiedad. Profesionales de atención primaria desconocían la regulación del sueño y el manejo del insomnio. La falta de sueño se vincula con la organización del trabajo y exige turnos protegidos, educación en higiene del sueño y programas de bienestar.

title: Efectividad de programas escolares para prevenir el suicidio en adolescentes: revisión sistemática
abstractText: Se evaluó la efectividad de los programas escolares para prevenir el suicidio en adolescentes. Se realizó una revisión sistemática según PRISMA en Scopus, SciELO y PubMed, con búsqueda complementaria, de estudios publicados entre 2019 y 2024; de 47 registros se incluyeron 12 estudios. Los factores de riesgo descritos fueron sexo femenino, edad menor de 16 años, clima familiar desfavorable, baja autoestima e inteligencia emocional, depresión, ansiedad, acoso escolar y consumo de alcohol y otras sustancias; el bienestar psicológico actuó como factor protector. Una revisión de 20 programas los asoció con menor ideación suicida y mayor confianza y conocimiento para buscar ayuda. En urgencias pediátricas españolas, los casos de suicidio, intento o ideación aumentaron un 56 %. Los programas escolares que combinan educación en salud mental, capacitación del personal y detección temprana reducen la ideación suicida; su efecto depende de la implementación y el seguimiento.

title: Miopía y astigmatismo por dispositivos electrónicos en niños y adolescentes desde la pandemia: revisión sistemática
abstractText: Se determinaron los factores de riesgo de miopía y astigmatismo en niños y adolescentes desde la pandemia de COVID-19. Se realizó una revisión sistemática según PRISMA 2020 en cinco bases de datos (2019-2024); de 73 registros se preseleccionaron 11 y seis cumplieron los criterios tras la revisión del texto completo. El uso de pantallas durante más de 2 horas diarias duplicó el riesgo de miopía, el antecedente familiar lo multiplicó por 1,9 y la exposición solar mayor de 2 horas fue protectora. La progresión fue mayor con más de 3 horas de pantalla y menos de 1 hora de sol. El astigmatismo miópico fue la ametropía más frecuente en escolares (63,7 %) y el síndrome visual informático afectó al 93 % de universitarios en clases virtuales. Limitar el tiempo de pantalla, promover las actividades al aire libre y realizar controles visuales periódicos son medidas preventivas para enfermería.

title: Ortodoncia preventiva en niños: aparatos funcionales, expansores palatinos y mantenedores de espacio
abstractText: Esta revisión analizó la evidencia sobre la eficacia y la estabilidad de los aparatos funcionales, los expansores palatinos y los mantenedores de espacio en la ortodoncia preventiva infantil. Se realizó una revisión narrativa en PubMed, Scopus y Google Académico, que incluyó 15 ensayos clínicos, estudios observacionales, revisiones sistemáticas y consensos. Los hábitos de succión y la deglución atípica se asociaron con maloclusión. La expansión maxilar corrigió la mordida cruzada posterior y mejoró la calidad de vida; la máscara facial redujo la necesidad de cirugía ortognática en la clase III, con recidiva parcial; los aparatos funcionales de clase II mostraron efectos principalmente dentoalveolares. La evidencia sobre mantenedores de espacio fue escasa. La ortodoncia preventiva es eficaz en indicaciones específicas y requiere estudios longitudinales que confirmen su estabilidad.

title: Educación sanitaria para la prevención de infecciones de transmisión sexual en adolescentes: revisión narrativa
abstractText: Se analizó la efectividad de la educación sanitaria en la prevención de infecciones de transmisión sexual en adolescentes. Se realizó una revisión narrativa de la literatura en PubMed, SciELO y Google Académico; se incluyeron 10 estudios publicados entre 2018 y 2024. Los estudios transversales mostraron conocimientos intermedios o bajos, conductas de riesgo frecuentes y disfunción familiar en adolescentes con estas infecciones. Las intervenciones educativas elevaron el conocimiento sobre vías de transmisión y prevención; en Palma Soriano, el conocimiento bueno llegó al 96,1 %. Un metaanálisis de 63 estudios halló efectos a corto plazo que se atenuaron con el tiempo y un mayor uso del preservativo a largo plazo; los programas con participación de los padres mejoraron el uso del preservativo y la comunicación familiar. La educación sanitaria mejora el conocimiento y las prácticas preventivas; su efecto requiere continuidad, participación familiar y liderazgo de enfermería en la escuela.

title: Hábitos de higiene y prevención de enfermedades en escolares de la Unidad Educativa «César Borja»
abstractText: Se buscó determinar los hábitos de higiene y las prácticas de prevención de enfermedades en niños de tercer y cuarto grado de la Unidad Educativa «César Borja», parroquia rural de Ambuquí, Ecuador. Se realizó un estudio cuantitativo, no experimental, transversal y descriptivo con los 30 niños de ambos grados, mediante un cuestionario de 10 preguntas cerradas. El 60,0 % se lava siempre las manos antes de comer y el 40,0 % solo a veces; el 56,7 % se las lava siempre después de ir al baño. El 66,7 % se cepilla siempre los dientes después de cada comida y el 56,7 % se baña siempre a diario. El 66,7 % refirió enfermarse «siempre». Los niños refieren prácticas de higiene frecuentes, pero no constantes. Conviene reforzar la educación en higiene con docentes y padres de familia y asegurar insumos básicos en la escuela.

title: Factores epidemiológicos asociados con enfermedades cardiovasculares en adultos mayores: revisión narrativa
abstractText: Se identificaron los factores epidemiológicos asociados con las enfermedades cardiovasculares en adultos mayores. Se realizó una revisión narrativa de ocho estudios observacionales de 2013 a 2023 indizados en PubMed, SciELO y Redalyc, procedentes de España, Perú, Cuba, Brasil y Estados Unidos. La hipertensión arterial afectó entre el 44,1 % y el 67,2 % de los participantes, la obesidad abdominal llegó al 77,6 %, el sedentarismo al 59,7 % y el síndrome metabólico al 78,9 % en mujeres; el 13,1 % de los octogenarios acumuló tres o más factores. La fragilidad, la multimorbilidad, el bajo ingreso, la falta de apoyo familiar y la atención discontinua se asociaron con la mortalidad cardiovascular, y caminar a paso rápido redujo a la mitad el riesgo coronario y de ictus. Las enfermedades cardiovasculares del adulto mayor dependen de factores clásicos que coexisten y de condiciones geriátricas y sociales que enfermería puede detectar y controlar.

title: Trastornos alimenticios en estudiantes de segundo año de bachillerato de la Unidad Educativa Tulcán
abstractText: Se identificaron actitudes y conductas relacionadas con los trastornos alimenticios en estudiantes de segundo año de bachillerato de la Unidad Educativa Tulcán, Ecuador. Se realizó un estudio cuantitativo, descriptivo, no experimental y transversal con la población total de 119 estudiantes, que respondió un cuestionario estructurado de 26 preguntas cerradas con escala de frecuencia. El 21,8 % sentía siempre angustia ante la idea de estar demasiado gordo o gorda, el 8,4 % muy a menudo y el 29,4 % a menudo. El 3,4 % procuraba siempre no comer pese a tener hambre y el 26,1 % lo hacía a menudo. El 8,4 % refirió crisis de atracones siempre y el 51,3 % nunca. El 5,0 % se sentía siempre culpable después de comer; el 3,4 % hacía dieta siempre y el 36,1 % nunca. La preocupación por el peso y las conductas restrictivas respaldan acciones escolares de prevención y detección temprana.

title: Impacto de la dependencia de la inteligencia artificial en la educación de adolescentes: revisión narrativa
abstractText: Se analizó el efecto de la dependencia de la inteligencia artificial en el aprendizaje de adolescentes y estudiantes jóvenes. Se realizó una revisión narrativa en PubMed, SciELO y Google Académico; se sintetizaron seis estudios primarios y una revisión sistemática publicados en 2024. Entre el 14,8 % y el 52,6 % de los adolescentes usaba IA generativa para tareas escolares, y quienes tenían más dificultades de función ejecutiva la consideraban más útil. La dependencia afectó al 17,14 % y luego al 24,19 % de 3 843 adolescentes, y los problemas emocionales la precedieron. En universitarios, el estrés académico y la carga de trabajo se asociaron con mayor uso, procrastinación, pérdida de memoria y menor rendimiento; la dependencia excesiva redujo el pensamiento crítico y el razonamiento analítico. La IA aporta apoyo y personalización, pero su uso sin guía pedagógica limita la autonomía y el pensamiento crítico de los estudiantes.

title: Factores de riesgo para la salud mental de estudiantes de externado de enfermería, UNIANDES-Tulcán
abstractText: Se analizaron los factores de riesgo para la salud mental de los estudiantes de externado de enfermería de UNIANDES, sede Tulcán. Estudio cuantitativo, descriptivo, no experimental y transversal, en la población de 131 estudiantes de tercero a séptimo nivel, mediante un cuestionario de 15 preguntas cerradas. El 51,9 % adoptó una postura neutral sobre el efecto de la carga horaria en su salud mental y el 29,6 % la consideró perjudicial. El 40,0 % refirió impacto emocional por el contacto con pacientes críticos, el 68,1 % rara vez o nunca tuvo tiempo para el descanso y el autocuidado, el 53,4 % temió siempre o casi siempre cometer errores por estrés o fatiga y el 16,3 % sintió ansiedad en todos los turnos. La falta de descanso, el temor a equivocarse y la exigencia emocional respaldan programas institucionales de apoyo psicológico y manejo del estrés.
